title.zh: 卷四十二 列傳第二 劉穆之 王弘
title.en: Volume 42 Biographies 2: Liu Muzhi, Wang Hong
title.raw: 卷四十二 列傳第二 劉穆之 王弘 Volume 42 Biographies 2: Liu Muzhi, Wang Hong

sentences.zh: 列傳第二 劉穆之 王弘

translations.literal: Biographies 2: Liu Muzhi, Wang Hong
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 2: Liu Muzhi and Wang Hong

sentences.zh: 劉穆之，字道和，小字道民，東莞莒人，漢齊悼惠王肥後也。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi, style name Daohe, childhood name Daomin, was a native of Ju in Dongguan and a descendant of Prince Fei the Lamented and Kind of Qi of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi, whose style name was Daohe and childhood name Daomin, came from Ju in Dongguan and was descended from Prince Fei the Lamented and Kind of Qi of Han.

sentences.zh: 世居京口。

translations.literal: His family had long resided at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived at Jingkou for generations.

sentences.zh: 少好書、傳，博覽多通，為濟陽江敳所知。

translations.literal: In youth he loved the classics and commentaries, read widely and mastered much, and came to the notice of Jiang Ai of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved the classics and their commentaries, read widely with deep understanding, and won the recognition of Jiang Ai of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 敳為建武將軍、琅邪內史，以為府主簿。

translations.literal: When Ai served as General Who Establishes Martial Might and Interior Minister of Langye, he appointed him chief clerk of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Ai held the posts of General Who Establishes Martial Might and interior minister of Langye, he made Muzhi chief clerk of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，穆之嘗夢與高祖俱泛海，忽值大風，驚懼。

translations.literal: Earlier, Muzhi had once dreamed that he and the Founding Emperor were sailing the sea together when suddenly a great wind arose, and he was startled and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Muzhi once dreamed that he and Emperor Gaozu were sailing the open sea together when a sudden gale struck, filling him with alarm.

sentences.zh: 俯視船下，見有二白龍夾舫。

translations.literal: Looking down beneath the boat, he saw two white dragons flanking the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: When he looked down from the boat, he saw two white dragons flanking the vessel on either side.

sentences.zh: 既而至一山，峯㠋聳秀，林樹繁密，意甚悅之。

translations.literal: Presently they came to a mountain whose peaks rose towering and fair, with dense woods and trees, and he was greatly pleased in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they reached a mountain whose peaks rose steep and graceful, its woods thick and lush, and he felt deep delight.

sentences.zh: 及高祖克京城，問何無忌曰：「急須一府主簿，何由得之？」

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor took the capital, he asked He Wuji, "I urgently need a chief clerk for headquarters — how am I to obtain one?"
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozu captured the capital, he asked He Wuji, "I urgently need a chief clerk for headquarters. How can I find the right man?"

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「無過劉道民。」

translations.literal: Wuji said, "None better than Liu Daomin."
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji replied, "No one better than Liu Daomin."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「吾亦識之。」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "I know him as well."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "I know him too."

sentences.zh: 即馳信召焉。

translations.literal: He at once sent a swift messenger to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent a fast courier to summon him.

sentences.zh: 時穆之聞京城有叫譟之聲，晨起出陌頭，屬與信會。

translations.literal: At that time Muzhi had heard shouting and clamor in the capital; rising early he went out to the roadside, and just then met the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi had heard shouting and uproar in the capital; rising early he went out to the roadside, where he happened upon the courier.

sentences.zh: 穆之直視不言者久之。

translations.literal: Muzhi stared straight ahead and said nothing for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi fixed his gaze ahead and remained silent for a long while.

sentences.zh: 既而反室，壞布裳為絝，往見高祖。

translations.literal: Then he returned indoors, tore his cloth robe to make trousers, and went to see the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went back inside, ripped his cloth robe to fashion trousers, and went to see Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂之曰：「我始舉大義，方造艱難，須一軍吏甚急，卿謂誰堪其選？」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor said to him, "I have just raised the great cause and am entering hardship; I urgently need a military clerk — whom do you think fit for the post?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said to him, "I have just raised the great enterprise and am entering hard times. I urgently need a military clerk. Whom do you think is fit for the post?"

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「貴府始建，軍吏實須其才，倉卒之際，當略無見踰者。」

translations.literal: Muzhi said, "Your headquarters is newly founded and truly needs talent for a military clerk; in this hurried moment, there is scarcely anyone who surpasses me."
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi replied, "Your headquarters is only now being established and truly needs a capable military clerk. In this hurried moment, there is scarcely anyone who surpasses me."

sentences.zh: 高祖笑曰：「卿能自屈，吾事濟矣。」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor laughed and said, "If you can humble yourself thus, my cause is assured."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu laughed and said, "If you can humble yourself in this way, my cause is assured."

sentences.zh: 即於坐受署。

translations.literal: He was appointed on the spot where they sat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 從平京邑，高祖始至，諸大處分，皆倉卒立定，並穆之所建也。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of the capital region, when the Founding Emperor first arrived, all major arrangements were settled in haste — all were Muzhi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was pacified and Emperor Gaozu first arrived, every major disposition was settled in haste, and all of it was Muzhi's work.

sentences.zh: 遂委以腹心之任，動止咨焉。

translations.literal: He was then entrusted with duties of the innermost heart; in movement and rest the Emperor consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then entrusted with the emperor's innermost confidence, and Gaozu consulted him in every move he made.

sentences.zh: 穆之亦竭節盡誠，無所遺隱。

translations.literal: Muzhi also exhausted his integrity and gave his utmost loyalty, concealing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi, for his part, gave his utmost loyalty and held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 時晉綱寬弛，威禁不行，盛族豪右，負勢陵縱，小民窮蹙，自立無所。

translations.literal: At that time the bonds of Jin were lax and slack, awe and prohibition did not prevail, great clans and powerful houses relied on force to bully and indulge themselves, and common people were pressed to destitution with nowhere to stand on their own.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the authority of Jin had grown lax, and law could not be enforced. Great clans and powerful houses bullied others at will, while common people were driven to destitution with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 重以司馬元顯政令違舛，桓玄科條繁密。

translations.literal: Added to this, Sima Yuanxian's government orders were perverse and mistaken, while Huan Xuan's statutes were numerous and tight.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this, Sima Yuanxian's edicts were erratic and contradictory, while Huan Xuan's regulations were numerous and oppressive.

sentences.zh: 穆之斟酌時宜，隨方矯正，不盈旬日，風俗頓改。

translations.literal: Muzhi weighed the needs of the time and corrected matters as each case required; within less than ten days customs changed abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi weighed the needs of the moment and corrected abuses as each case required. In less than ten days the customs of the region were transformed.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書祠部郎，復為府主簿，記室錄事參軍，領堂邑太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites in the Masters of Writing, again served as chief clerk of headquarters, recording secretary and registrar staff officer, and concurrently held the post of grand administrator of Tangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman of the Ministry of Rites in the Masters of Writing, again made chief clerk of headquarters and recording secretary with registrar duties, and concurrently served as grand administrator of Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 以平桓玄功，封西華縣五等子。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying Huan Xuan he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Viscount of Xihua county.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in suppressing Huan Xuan he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Viscount of Xihua.

sentences.zh: 義熙三年，揚州刺史王謐薨，高祖次應入輔，劉毅等不欲高祖入，議以中領軍謝混為揚州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi, Grand Administrator of Yangzhou Wang Mi died; the Founding Emperor was next in line to enter as chief minister, but Liu Yi and others did not wish him to enter and debated making Central Commander of the Army Xie Hun governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yixi, when Grand Administrator of Yangzhou Wang Mi died, Emperor Gaozu was next in line to enter the capital as chief minister. Liu Yi and others did not want him to do so and proposed making Central Commander of the Army Xie Hun governor of Yangzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 或欲令高祖於丹徒領州，以內事付尚書僕射孟昶。

translations.literal: Some wished to have the Founding Emperor hold the province from Dantu while entrusting internal affairs to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Meng Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Others wanted Emperor Gaozu to hold the province from Dantu while turning internal affairs over to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Meng Chang.

sentences.zh: 遣尚書右丞皮沈以二議咨高祖。

translations.literal: They sent Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Pi Shen to consult the Founding Emperor on the two proposals.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Pi Shen to present both proposals to Emperor Gaozu for his view.

sentences.zh: 沈先見穆之，具說朝議。

translations.literal: Shen first saw Muzhi and fully explained the court deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Shen first met with Muzhi and explained the court deliberations in full.

sentences.zh: 穆之偽起如廁，即密疏白高祖曰：「皮沈始至，其言不可從。」

translations.literal: Muzhi pretended to rise as if for the privy and at once sent a secret memorial informing the Founding Emperor, "Pi Shen has only just arrived; his words must not be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi pretended to rise as if for the privy and at once sent a secret note to Emperor Gaozu: "Pi Shen has only just arrived. His proposal must not be accepted."

sentences.zh: 高祖既見沈，且令出外，呼穆之問曰：「卿云沈言不可從，其意何也？」

translations.literal: After the Founding Emperor had seen Shen and sent him out for the moment, he summoned Muzhi and asked, "You say Shen's words must not be followed — what is your meaning?"
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozu had seen Shen and sent him out for the moment, he summoned Muzhi and asked, "You say Shen's proposal must not be accepted. What do you mean by that?"

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「昔晉朝失政，非復一日，加以桓玄篡奪，天命已移。

translations.literal: Muzhi said, "Formerly the Jin court lost good government — this was not a matter of a single day — and moreover Huan Xuan usurped power; the Mandate had already shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi said, "The Jin court lost its way long ago, and that was not a matter of a single day. Then Huan Xuan seized power, and the Mandate had already shifted.

sentences.zh: 公興復皇祚，勳高萬古。

translations.literal: Your Lordship has restored the imperial line; your merit towers above ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your Lordship has restored the imperial house, and your merit towers above ten thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 既有大功，便有大位。

translations.literal: Having great merit, you should hold great position.
translations.idiomatic: Having achieved great merit, you ought to hold great position.

sentences.zh: 位大勳高，非可持久。

translations.literal: Great position and towering merit cannot long endure together in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Great position and towering merit cannot long endure in this arrangement.

sentences.zh: 公今日形勢，豈得居謙自弱，遂為守藩之將邪？

translations.literal: Given Your Lordship's situation today, how can you dwell in modesty and weaken yourself, becoming merely a general who guards a border province?
translations.idiomatic: Given your position today, how can you remain modest and weaken yourself until you become nothing more than a frontier commander guarding a border province?

sentences.zh: 劉、孟諸公，與公俱起布衣，共立大義，本欲匡主成勳，以取富貴耳。

translations.literal: Lords Liu, Meng, and the rest rose with you from common cloth, together raised the great cause, and originally meant only to support the ruler and win merit so as to gain wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu, Meng, and the others rose with you from common cloth, raised the great cause together, and originally meant only to restore the ruler and win merit so as to gain wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 事有前後，故一時推功，非為委體心服，宿定臣主之分也。

translations.literal: Matters have an order of precedence, so for a time they yielded merit to you — not because they had surrendered body and heart in lasting submission or because the division of lord and minister had been fixed long before.
translations.idiomatic: Matters have their order of precedence, so for a time they yielded merit to you. That was not because they had surrendered body and heart in lasting submission, or because the bond of lord and minister had been fixed long before.

sentences.zh: 力敵勢均，終相吞咀。

translations.literal: When strength is matched and power equal, in the end they devour one another.
translations.idiomatic: When strength is matched and power equal, in the end they will devour one another.

sentences.zh: 揚州根本所係，不可假人。

translations.literal: Yangzhou is where the root foundation lies; it cannot be lent to another.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou is where the root foundation lies. It cannot be entrusted to another.

sentences.zh: 前者以授王謐，事出權道，豈是始終大計必宜若此而已哉。

translations.literal: Earlier it was given to Wang Mi — that arose from expedient policy; how could that be the enduring grand design, necessarily to be done thus and no more?
translations.idiomatic: Giving it earlier to Wang Mi was an expedient measure. How could that be the enduring grand design, necessarily to be done thus forever?

sentences.zh: 今若復以他授，便應受制於人。

translations.literal: If it is now given again to someone else, you will at once fall under another's control.
translations.idiomatic: If you now hand it to someone else again, you will at once fall under another man's control.

sentences.zh: 一失權柄，無由可得。

translations.literal: Once authority is lost, there is no way to regain it.
translations.idiomatic: Once you lose authority, there will be no way to regain it.

sentences.zh: 而公功高勳重，不可直置，疑畏交加，異端互起，將來之危難，可不熟念。

translations.literal: Yet Your Lordship's merit is high and your honors weighty — you cannot simply be set aside. Suspicion and fear will press upon one another, strange factions will rise in turn, and future dangers and hardships — can these not be pondered with care?
translations.idiomatic: Yet your merit is high and your honors weighty; you cannot simply be set aside. Suspicion and fear will press upon one another, strange factions will rise in turn, and the dangers ahead — can you not ponder them with care?

sentences.zh: 今朝議如此，宜相酬答，必云在我，厝辭又難。

translations.literal: Today's court deliberation is thus; you should answer in kind. To say outright that you want it yourself would make phrasing difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Today's court deliberation runs as it does. You should answer in kind. To say outright that you want the post yourself would make the wording difficult.

sentences.zh: 唯應云『神州治本，宰輔崇要，興喪所階，宜加詳擇。

translations.literal: You should only say, "The capital region is the root of the realm; chief ministers hold honored importance; rise and fall depend on this step — the choice should receive careful deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: You should only say, "The capital region is the root of the realm, and chief ministers hold honored importance. The rise and fall of the state depend on this appointment, and the choice should receive careful deliberation."

sentences.zh: 此事既大，非可懸論，便暫入朝，共盡同異』。

translations.literal: This matter is already great and cannot be debated at a distance; let me enter court for a time so we may together exhaust agreement and difference."
translations.idiomatic: This matter is too great to debate at a distance. Let me enter court for a time so we may together settle agreement and difference."

sentences.zh: 公至京，彼必不敢越公更授餘人明矣。」

translations.literal: When Your Lordship reaches the capital, they will certainly not dare to pass you by and give the post to someone else — that is clear."
translations.idiomatic: When you reach the capital, they will certainly not dare to pass you by and give the post to someone else. That much is clear."

sentences.zh: 高祖從其言，由是入輔。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor followed his words and thereby entered as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu followed his advice and thereby entered the capital as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 從征廣固，還拒盧循，常居幙中畫策，決斷眾事。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Guanggu and returning to resist Lu Xun, he constantly dwelt within the command tent drafting plans and deciding the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Guanggu and in the defense against Lu Xun, he constantly worked within the command tent drafting plans and deciding every major affair.

sentences.zh: 劉毅等疾穆之見親，每從容言其權重，高祖愈信仗之。

translations.literal: Liu Yi and others resented Muzhi's favored intimacy; each time they spoke at leisure of his weight of power, and the Founding Emperor trusted and relied on him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi and others resented Muzhi's favored intimacy. Whenever they spoke at leisure of his excessive power, Emperor Gaozu trusted and relied on him all the more.

sentences.zh: 穆之外所聞見，莫不大小必白，雖復閭里言謔，塗陌細事，皆一二以聞。

translations.literal: Whatever Muzhi heard or saw outside, whether great or small he always reported; even village jest and roadside trifles he recounted one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Muzhi heard or saw outside, great or small, he always reported. Even village gossip and roadside trifles he recounted one by one.

sentences.zh: 高祖每得民間委密消息以示聰明，皆由穆之也。

translations.literal: Whenever the Founding Emperor obtained confidential news from among the people to display his keen intelligence, it all came through Muzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Gaozu obtained confidential news from among the people to display his keen intelligence, it all came through Muzhi.

sentences.zh: 又愛好賓遊，坐客恒滿，布耳目以為視聽，故朝野同異，穆之莫不必知。

translations.literal: He also loved to entertain guests; seated visitors were always full, and he spread eyes and ears as his means of seeing and hearing, so that whatever differed in court and countryside Muzhi invariably knew.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved to entertain guests, and his hall was always full. He spread eyes and ears throughout the realm, so that whatever differed in court and countryside Muzhi invariably knew.

sentences.zh: 雖復親暱短長，皆陳奏無隱。

translations.literal: Even the faults and merits of those close and dear he presented in memorial without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Even the faults and merits of those close to the emperor he reported without concealment.

sentences.zh: 人或譏之，穆之曰：「以公之明，將來會自聞達。

translations.literal: Some ridiculed him for it. Muzhi said, "Given Your Lordship's keen intelligence, in time you will hear of these things yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Some ridiculed him for it. Muzhi said, "Given your keen intelligence, in time you will hear of these things yourself.

sentences.zh: 我蒙公恩，義無隱諱，此張遼所以告關羽欲叛也。」

translations.literal: I have received Your Lordship's grace; by right I cannot conceal — this is why Zhang Liao reported to Guan Yu that someone wished to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: I have received your grace. By right I cannot conceal anything. That is why Zhang Liao reported to Guan Yu that someone wished to rebel."

sentences.zh: 高祖舉止施為，穆之皆下節度。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor's conduct and actions Muzhi all regulated from below.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu's conduct and actions Muzhi all regulated from below.

sentences.zh: 高祖書素拙，穆之曰：「此雖小事，然宣彼四遠，願公小復留意。」

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor's handwriting was by nature clumsy. Muzhi said, "Though this is a small matter, it is proclaimed to the four quarters and far regions — I hope Your Lordship will give it a little attention again."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu's handwriting was by nature clumsy. Muzhi said, "Though this is a small matter, it is proclaimed to the four quarters. I hope Your Lordship will give it a little attention."

sentences.zh: 高祖既不能厝意，又稟分有在。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor could neither set his mind to it nor alter what nature had allotted him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu could neither set his mind to it nor alter what nature had allotted him.

sentences.zh: 穆之乃曰：「但縱筆為大字，一字徑尺，無嫌。

translations.literal: Muzhi then said, "Simply let the brush run in large characters — one character a foot across — and there is no fault.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi then said, "Simply let the brush run in large characters, one character a foot across, and there is no fault.

sentences.zh: 大既足有所包，且其勢亦美。」

translations.literal: Large characters are sufficient to contain meaning, and their force is also beautiful."
translations.idiomatic: Large characters are sufficient to contain meaning, and their force is also beautiful."

sentences.zh: [1]高祖從之，一紙不過六七字便滿。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor followed this; a single sheet held no more than six or seven characters before it was full.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu followed this advice, and a single sheet held no more than six or seven characters before it was full.

sentences.zh: 凡所薦達，不進不止，常云：「我雖不及荀令君之舉善，然不舉不善。」

translations.literal: Of all he recommended for advancement, he did not stop until they were promoted, and he often said, "Though I do not match Director Ling of Xun in recommending the good, I do not recommend the unworthy."
translations.idiomatic: Of all he recommended for advancement, he did not stop until they were promoted. He often said, "Though I do not match Director Ling of Xun in recommending the worthy, I never recommend the unworthy."

sentences.zh: 穆之與朱齡石並便尺牘，嘗於高祖坐與齡石答書。

translations.literal: Muzhi and Zhu Lingshi were both adept at letters. Once, in the Founding Emperor's presence, Muzhi and Lingshi answered correspondence together.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi and Zhu Lingshi were both adept at correspondence. Once, in Emperor Gaozu's presence, Muzhi and Lingshi answered letters together.

sentences.zh: 自旦至日中，[2]穆之得百函，齡石得八十函，而穆之應對無廢也。

translations.literal: From dawn until midday, Muzhi handled a hundred bundles and Lingshi eighty, yet Muzhi's replies showed no lapse.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn until midday, Muzhi handled a hundred bundles and Lingshi eighty, yet Muzhi's replies never faltered.

sentences.zh: 轉中軍太尉司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Major of the Army of the Central Army and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to major of the army under the Central Army and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 八年，加丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was additionally made Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was additionally made intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖西討劉毅，以諸葛長民監留府，總攝後事。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor marched west to attack Liu Yi, he placed Zhuge Changmin in charge of the rear headquarters to oversee all subsequent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu marched west to attack Liu Yi, he placed Zhuge Changmin in charge of the rear headquarters to oversee all subsequent affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖疑長民難獨任，留穆之以輔之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor doubted that Changmin could bear the burden alone and left Muzhi behind to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu doubted that Changmin could bear the burden alone and left Muzhi behind to assist him.

sentences.zh: 加建威將軍，置佐吏，配給實力。

translations.literal: Muzhi was given the additional title General Who Establishes Martial Might, with staff officers appointed and substantive forces allotted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi was given the additional title General Who Establishes Martial Might, with staff officers appointed and substantive forces allotted to him.

sentences.zh: 長民果有異謀，而猶豫不能發，乃屏人謂穆之曰：「悠悠之言，皆云太尉與我不平，何以至此？」

translations.literal: Changmin did harbor a different design, yet hesitated and could not act; he dismissed attendants and said to Muzhi, "Loose talk everywhere says the Grand Commandant and I are at odds — how has it come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Changmin did harbor a different design, yet hesitated and could not act. He dismissed attendants and said to Muzhi, "Loose talk everywhere says the Grand Commandant and I are at odds. How has it come to this?"

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「公泝流遠伐，而以老母稚子委節下，若一毫不盡，豈容如此邪？」

translations.literal: Muzhi said, "Your Lordship is campaigning far upstream while entrusting your aged mother and young children to his command — if he failed in the slightest, how could matters stand thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi replied, "Your Lordship is campaigning far upstream while entrusting your aged mother and young children to his command. If he failed in the slightest, how could matters stand thus?"

sentences.zh: 意乃小安。

translations.literal: His mind was somewhat eased.
translations.idiomatic: His mind was somewhat eased.

sentences.zh: 高祖還，長民伏誅。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor returned, Changmin was executed where he lay prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu returned, Changmin was executed.

sentences.zh: 十年，進穆之前將軍，給前軍府年布萬匹，錢三百萬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Muzhi was advanced to Forward General and granted ten thousand bolts of annual cloth for the Forward Army headquarters and three million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Muzhi was advanced to Forward General and granted ten thousand bolts of annual cloth for the Forward Army headquarters and three million in cash.

sentences.zh: 十一年，高祖西伐司馬休之，中軍將軍道憐知留任，而事無大小，一決穆之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Founding Emperor marched west against Sima Xiuzhi; Central Army General Daolin nominally held the rear post, yet in affairs great and small Muzhi alone decided.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Emperor Gaozu marched west against Sima Xiuzhi. Central Army General Daolin nominally held the rear post, yet in affairs great and small Muzhi alone decided.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右僕射，領選，將軍、尹如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with charge of selection; his generalship and intendancy remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice director of the Masters of Writing with charge of selection, while his generalship and intendancy remained as before.

sentences.zh: 十二年，高祖北伐，留世子為中軍將軍，監太尉留府；

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Founding Emperor marched north; he left the heir as Central Army General to oversee the rear headquarters of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Emperor Gaozu marched north. He left the heir as central army general to oversee the rear headquarters of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 轉穆之左僕射，領監軍、中軍二府軍司，將軍、尹、領選如故。

translations.literal: Muzhi was transferred to Left Vice Director, concurrently overseeing the military supervisors of the Supervisory Army and Central Army headquarters; his generalship, intendancy, and charge of selection remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi was transferred to left vice director, concurrently overseeing the military supervisors of the Supervisory Army and Central Army headquarters, while his generalship, intendancy, and charge of selection remained as before.

sentences.zh: [3]甲仗五十人，入殿。

translations.literal: [3] Fifty armed guards were granted him with permission to enter the hall.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He was granted fifty armed guards with permission to enter the hall.

sentences.zh: [4]入居東城。

translations.literal: [4] He took up residence in the Eastern City.
translations.idiomatic: [4] He took up residence in the Eastern City.

sentences.zh: 穆之內總朝政，外供軍旅，決斷如流，事無擁滯。

translations.literal: Within, Muzhi oversaw court government; without, he supplied the armies. His decisions flowed like water, and no affair piled up in obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Within, Muzhi oversaw court government; without, he supplied the armies. His decisions flowed like water, and no affair piled up in delay.

sentences.zh: 賓客輻輳，求訴百端，內外諮稟，盈堦滿室，目覽辭訟，手答牋書，耳行聽受，口並酬應，不相參涉，皆悉贍舉。

translations.literal: Guests converged like wheel spokes; petitions came by the hundred paths. Memorials from within and without filled the steps and packed the rooms. With his eyes he scanned lawsuits, with his hands answered letters, with his ears he took in reports on the move, with his mouth he answered all at once — none interfering with another — and all were fully handled.
translations.idiomatic: Guests converged in crowds, and petitions came by the hundred paths. Memorials from within and without filled the steps and packed the rooms. With his eyes he scanned lawsuits, with his hands answered letters, with his ears he took in reports on the move, and with his mouth he answered all at once, none interfering with another, and all were fully handled.

sentences.zh: 又數客暱賓，言談賞笑，引日亘時，未嘗倦苦。

translations.literal: Again and again he entertained close guests in talk, appreciation, and laughter, drawing out day across hours, never weary or suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he entertained close guests in conversation, wit, and laughter, drawing out the day across hours, never weary or suffering.

sentences.zh: 裁有閑暇，自手寫書，尋覽篇章，校定墳籍。

translations.literal: When he had a little leisure he copied books with his own hand, searched through chapters and sections, and collated canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: When he had a little leisure he copied books with his own hand, searched through chapters and sections, and collated canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 性奢豪，食必方丈，旦輒為十人饌。

translations.literal: By nature he was extravagant and grand; his meals always filled a square zhang, and each morning he had food prepared for ten men.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant and grand. His meals always filled a square zhang, and each morning he had food prepared for ten men.

sentences.zh: 穆之既好賓客，未嘗獨餐，每至食時，客止十人以還者，帳下依常下食，以此為常。

translations.literal: Since Muzhi loved guests he never dined alone; whenever mealtime came, if guests numbered no more than ten, his staff still served the regular full meal — this was his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: Since Muzhi loved guests he never dined alone. Whenever mealtime came, even if guests numbered no more than ten, his staff still served the regular full meal. This was his constant practice.

sentences.zh: 嘗白高祖曰：「穆之家本貧賤，贍生多闕。

translations.literal: He once reported to the Founding Emperor, "Muzhi's family was originally poor and lowly, and support for life was often lacking.
translations.idiomatic: He once reported to Emperor Gaozu, "Muzhi's family was originally poor and lowly, and support for daily life was often lacking.

sentences.zh: 自叨忝以來，雖每存約損，而朝夕所須，微為過豐。

translations.literal: Since receiving undeserved favor, though I have each time sought restraint and reduction, what is needed morning and evening is slightly excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Since receiving undeserved favor, though I have each time sought restraint, what is needed morning and evening is slightly excessive.

sentences.zh: 自此以外，一毫不以負公。」

translations.literal: Beyond this, not a hair's breadth have I failed Your Lordship."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, not a hair's breadth have I failed you."

sentences.zh: 十三年，疾篤，詔遣正直黃門郎問疾。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year his illness grew grave; an edict sent a Rectitude Gentleman of the Yellow Gate to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his illness grew grave, and an edict sent a rectitude gentleman of the Yellow Gate to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 十一月卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 高祖在長安，聞問驚慟，哀惋者數日。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was at Chang'an; on hearing the news he was startled and grieved, mourning in sorrow for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was at Chang'an. On hearing the news he was startled and grieved, mourning in sorrow for several days.

sentences.zh: 本欲頓駕關中，經略趙、魏。

translations.literal: He had originally intended to halt his carriage in Guanzhong and plan operations in Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally intended to halt in Guanzhong and plan operations in Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 穆之既卒，京邑任虛，乃馳還彭城，以司馬徐羨之代管留任，而朝廷大事常決穆之者，並悉北諮。

translations.literal: When Muzhi had died, the duties of the capital stood vacant; he galloped back to Pengcheng and had Secretariat Director Xu Xianzhi take over the rear post in his stead, while great affairs of court that Muzhi had regularly decided were all referred north for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzhi died, the duties of the capital stood vacant. Emperor Gaozu galloped back to Pengcheng and had Secretariat Director Xu Xianzhi take over the rear post, while great affairs of court that Muzhi had regularly decided were all referred north for consultation.

sentences.zh: 穆之前軍府文武二萬人，以三千配羨之建威府，餘悉配世子中軍府。

translations.literal: The civil and military staff of Muzhi's Forward Army headquarters numbered twenty thousand; three thousand were allotted to Xianzhi's Establish Martial Might headquarters, and the rest all to the heir's Central Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military staff of Muzhi's Forward Army headquarters numbered twenty thousand. Three thousand were allotted to Xianzhi's Establish Martial Might headquarters, and the rest all to the heir's Central Army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 追贈穆之散騎常侍、衞將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Posthumously Muzhi was enfeoffed as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Defender General, and Commissioner Equal to the Three Excellencies with an office of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Muzhi was enfeoffed as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, defender general, and commissioner equal to the three excellencies with an office of his own.

sentences.zh: 高祖又表天子曰：「臣聞崇賢旌善，王教所先；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu again memorialized the Son of Heaven, saying: "Your servant has heard that exalting the worthy and commending goodness come first in royal instruction;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu again memorialized the throne, saying: "I have heard that exalting the worthy and honoring goodness is the first duty of kings;

sentences.zh: 念功簡勞，義深追遠。

translations.literal: to recall meritorious service and select out labors — the principle of honoring the distant past runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: to remember service and mark out toil is the deepest form of reverence for the dead.

sentences.zh: 故司勳秉策，在勤必書；

translations.literal: Thus the Director of Merits holds the record; whoever labors must be written down;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Director of Merits keeps the register, and every act of service must be recorded;

sentences.zh: 德之休明，沒而彌著。

translations.literal: when virtue is splendid and bright, after death it shines all the more.
translations.idiomatic: when virtue is bright and good, after death it shines all the more.

sentences.zh: 故尚書左僕射、前將軍臣穆之，[5]爰自布衣，協佐義始，內端謀猷，外勤庶政，密勿軍國，心力俱盡。

translations.literal: The late Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Former General, your servant Muzhi,[5] from commoner status assisted from the beginning of righteous enterprise, inwardly setting plans straight, outwardly diligently handling general administration, confidentially attending to military and state affairs, exhausting both mind and strength.
translations.idiomatic: The late Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Former General, your servant Muzhi,[5] rose from commoner rank to assist from the very start of our righteous enterprise, setting plans straight within and diligently handling civil affairs without, attending confidentially to military and state matters until mind and strength were both spent.

sentences.zh: 及登庸朝右，尹司京畿，翼新王化，敷讚百揆。

translations.literal: When promoted to the right hand of court, he governed the capital region, assisted the new royal transformation, and spread praise through the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: When promoted to the right hand of court, he governed the capital region, assisted the new royal transformation, and lent his counsel to the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 頃戎車遠役，居中作扞，撫寄之勳，實洽朝野。

translations.literal: Recently, when war chariots went on distant campaigns, he remained at center as a bulwark; his achievements in caring for what was entrusted truly reached court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when the army marched on distant campaigns, he remained at the center as a bulwark; his achievements in holding what was entrusted truly won over court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 方宣讚盛猷，緝隆聖世，志績未究，遠邇悼心。

translations.literal: Just as he was about to proclaim and praise the great design and gather in the flourishing sage age, his intent and achievements had not been brought to completion, and near and far mourned in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to proclaim the great design and gather in a flourishing sage age, his intent and achievements were cut short, and near and far mourned him.

sentences.zh: 皇恩褒述，班同三事，榮哀兼備，寵靈已厚。

translations.literal: Imperial grace has lauded and described him, ranking him equal to the Three Excellencies; glory and mourning were both complete, and favor and distinction were already generous.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial grace has already praised and described him, ranking him with the Three Excellencies; glory and mourning were both complete, and favor was already generous.

sentences.zh: 臣伏思尋，自義熙草創，艱患未弭，外虞既殷，內難彌結，時屯世故，靡歲暫寧。

translations.literal: Your servant kneels in reflection: from the founding of Yixi, hardships and calamities had not been stilled; external anxieties were already pressing, internal troubles ever more tangled; the times were beset and affairs of the age dire — not a year passed in brief peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant reflects in submission: from the founding of Yixi, hardship and calamity had not ceased; external threats pressed in and internal troubles ever tightened; the times were beset and not a year passed in brief peace.

sentences.zh: 豈臣以寡乏，負荷國重，實賴穆之匡翼之益。

translations.literal: How could your servant, with meager inadequacy, bear the heavy burden of state? In truth it depended on Muzhi's benefit in correcting and assisting.
translations.idiomatic: How could I, with my meager inadequacy, bear the heavy burden of state? In truth I depended on Muzhi's counsel and support.

sentences.zh: 豈唯讜言嘉謀，溢于民聽；

translations.literal: Was it only that his forthright words and excellent counsel overflowed into what the people heard?
translations.idiomatic: Was it only that his forthright words and excellent counsel overflowed into public hearing?

sentences.zh: 若乃忠規遠畫，潛慮密謨，造膝詭辭，莫見其際。

translations.literal: As for loyal admonitions and far-reaching designs, hidden deliberations and secret strategies — words whispered at knee level in unfathomable phrasing — none could see their boundary.
translations.idiomatic: As for loyal admonitions and far-reaching designs, hidden deliberations and secret strategies — counsel whispered at the knee in words no one could fully fathom — none could see where they ended.

sentences.zh: 功隱於視聽，事隔於皇朝者，[6]不可稱記。

translations.literal: Achievements hidden from sight and hearing, affairs separated from the imperial court — [6] cannot be enumerated and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Achievements hidden from sight and hearing, affairs kept apart from the imperial court — [6] cannot be counted or recorded.

sentences.zh: 所以陳力一紀，克遂有成，出征入輔，幸不辱命，微夫人之左右，未有寧濟其事者矣。

translations.literal: Therefore, for a full twelve-year cycle he presented his strength and was able to accomplish success; going on campaign and entering to assist, fortunately he did not disgrace his commission — without this gentleman's guidance at hand, none could have brought those affairs peacefully to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, for a full twelve-year cycle he gave his strength and brought success; whether on campaign or in office, he did not disgrace his commission — without this gentleman's guidance at hand, none could have brought those affairs peacefully to completion.

sentences.zh: 履謙居寡，守之彌固，每議及封賞，輒深自抑絕。

translations.literal: He practiced humility and dwelt in fewness, guarding it ever more firmly; whenever discussion touched on enfeoffment and reward, he would deeply restrain and renounce it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced humility and dwelt in modesty, guarding it ever more firmly; whenever discussion touched on enfeoffment and reward, he deeply restrained and renounced it himself.

sentences.zh: 所以勳高當年，而未沾茅社，撫事永傷，胡寧可昧。

translations.literal: Thus, though his merit was high in his own age, he never received the benefit of fief and earth-altar sacrifice; handling the matter still wounds forever — how could one knowingly obscure it?
translations.idiomatic: Thus, though his merit was high in his own age, he never received fief and earth-altar sacrifice; to recall the matter still wounds forever — how could one knowingly obscure it?

sentences.zh: 謂宜加贈正司，追甄土宇，俾大賚所及，永秩於善人，忠正之烈，不泯於身後。

translations.literal: It is fitting to add posthumous gifts of the proper office, retrospectively grant territory, so that great rewards extend, a lasting rank to good men, and the fierce loyalty of the upright does not perish after death.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to add posthumous gifts of the proper office and retrospectively grant territory, so that great rewards may reach him, a lasting rank be given to a good man, and the loyalty of the upright not perish after death.

sentences.zh: 臣契闊屯泰，旋觀始終，金蘭之分，義深情密。

translations.literal: Your servant, through separation and abundance, adversity and ease, has looked back on beginning and end; the bond of gold and orchid — righteous and deep, affection close.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, through separation and reunion, adversity and ease, has looked back on beginning and end; our bond was righteous and deep, our affection close.

sentences.zh: 是以獻其乃懷，布之朝聽。」

translations.literal: Therefore I present his genuine heart and lay it before the court's hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I present what is in my heart and lay it before the court."

sentences.zh: 於是重贈侍中、司徒，封南昌縣侯，食邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was again posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanchang County with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Muzhi was again posthumously granted palace attendant and minister of education, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanchang County with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，思佐命元勳，詔曰：「故侍中、司徒南昌侯劉穆之，深謀遠猷，肇基王跡，勳造大業，誠實匪躬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, thinking of the founding ministers who aided fate, he issued an edict: "The late Palace Attendant, Minister of Education, and Marquis of Nanchang Liu Muzhi — deep counsel and far-reaching design, laying the foundation of the royal track, merit forging the great enterprise, sincere and devoted without sparing himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, thinking of the founding ministers who aided fate, he issued an edict: "The late palace attendant, minister of education, and Marquis of Nanchang Liu Muzhi — deep counsel and far-reaching design, laying the foundation of the royal enterprise, forging the great achievement with merit, sincere and devoted without sparing himself.

sentences.zh: 今理運惟新，蕃屏並肇，感事懷人，實深悽悼。

translations.literal: Now the governing fate is newly renewed, protective screens all newly established; moved by affairs and cherishing the man, the grief is truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: Now the governing order is newly renewed and protective screens all newly established; moved by affairs and cherishing the man, my grief is truly deep.

sentences.zh: 可進南康郡公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: He may be promoted to Duke of Nankang Commandery with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He may be promoted to Duke of Nankang Commandery with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 故左將軍、青州刺史王鎮惡，荊、郢之捷，剋翦放命，北伐之勳，參跡方叔。

translations.literal: The late Left General and Inspector of Qing Province Wang Zhen'e — in the victories at Jing and Ying he cut down the rebel command; in the merit of the northern campaign he matched the track of Fangshu.
translations.idiomatic: The late left general and inspector of Qing Province Wang Zhen'e — in the victories at Jing and Ying he cut down the rebel command; in the northern campaign his merit matched that of Fangshu.

sentences.zh: 念勤惟績，無忘厥心。

translations.literal: Recall his diligence and keep only his achievements; do not forget his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Recall his diligence and keep his achievements in mind; do not forget his devotion.

sentences.zh: 可進龍陽縣侯，增邑千五百戶。」

translations.literal: He may be promoted to Marquis of Longyang County with an increase of fifteen hundred households to his fief."
translations.idiomatic: He may be promoted to Marquis of Longyang County with an increase of fifteen hundred households to his fief."

sentences.zh: 諡穆之曰文宣公。

translations.literal: Muzhi was given the posthumous title Duke Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi was given the posthumous title Duke Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉九年，配食高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wu, he was allotted sacrificial food in Emperor Gaozu's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wu, he was allotted sacrificial food in Emperor Gaozu's temple court.

sentences.zh: 二十五年四月，車駕行幸江寧，經穆之墓，詔曰：「故侍中、司徒、南康文宣公穆之，秉德佐命，翼亮景業，謀猷經遠，元勳克茂，功銘鼎彝，義彰典策，故已嗣徽前哲，宣風後代者矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year, the imperial carriage traveled in favor to Jiangning and passed Muzhi's tomb. An edict read: "The late Palace Attendant, Minister of Education, and Duke Wenxuan of Nankang, Muzhi — upholding virtue and aiding fate, brightening and supporting the radiant enterprise, counsel and design spanning far, founding merit flourishing abundantly, his achievements inscribed on tripods and cauldrons, his righteousness manifest in canonical records — thus already succeeding and emulating former sages, spreading influence among later generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year, the imperial carriage traveled to Jiangning and passed Muzhi's tomb. An edict read: "The late palace attendant, minister of education, and Duke Wenxuan of Nankang, Muzhi — upholding virtue and aiding fate, brightening and supporting the radiant enterprise, counsel and design spanning far, founding merit flourishing abundantly, his achievements inscribed on tripods and cauldrons, his righteousness manifest in canonical records — thus already succeeding and emulating former sages and spreading influence among later generations.

sentences.zh: 近因遊踐，瞻其塋域，九原之想，情深悼歎。

translations.literal: Recently, while traveling on an excursion, I gazed upon his grave domain; thoughts of the Nine Plains — the grief deep, sighing with mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, while traveling on an excursion, I gazed upon his grave; thoughts of the Nine Plains stirred deep grief and mourning sighs.

sentences.zh: 可致祭墓所，以申永懷。」

translations.literal: Sacrifice may be performed at the tomb site to express everlasting remembrance."
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice may be performed at the tomb to express everlasting remembrance."

sentences.zh: 穆之三子，長子慮之嗣，仕至員外散騎常侍卒。

translations.literal: Muzhi had three sons. The eldest, Luzhi, succeeded and served up to Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi had three sons. The eldest, Luzhi, succeeded and served up to extraordinary regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, then died.

sentences.zh: 子邕嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 先是郡縣為封國者，內史、相並於國主稱臣，去任便止。

translations.literal: Previously, where commanderies and counties served as fief-states, the internal administrator and administrator both addressed the lord of the state as subject; when leaving office this ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, where commanderies and counties served as fief-states, the internal administrator and administrator both addressed the lord of the state as subject; when leaving office this ceased.

sentences.zh: 至世祖孝建中，始革此制，為下官致敬。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Xiaowu of Song in the Xiaojian period, this system was first reformed so that lower officials gave formal respect.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xiaojian period under Emperor Xiaowu, this system was first reformed so that lower officials gave formal respect.

sentences.zh: 河東王歆之嘗為南康相，素輕邕。

translations.literal: Prince of Hedong Xinzhi had once served as Administrator of Nankang and always looked down on Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hedong Xinzhi had once served as administrator of Nankang and always looked down on Yong.

sentences.zh: 後歆之與邕俱豫元會，並坐。

translations.literal: Later Xinzhi and Yong both attended the New Year's audience and sat together.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xinzhi and Yong both attended the New Year's audience and sat together.

sentences.zh: 邕性嗜酒，謂歆之曰：「卿昔嘗見臣，今不能見勸一盃酒乎？」

translations.literal: Yong was fond of wine by nature. He said to Xinzhi: "You once called yourself my subject — can you not now urge me to drink a cup of wine?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong was fond of wine by nature. He said to Xinzhi: "You once called yourself my subject — can you not now urge me to drink a cup of wine?"

sentences.zh: 歆之因斅孫晧歌答之曰：「昔為汝作臣，今與汝比肩。

translations.literal: Xinzhi, using Sun Hao's song in reply, answered: "Once I was your subject; now I stand shoulder to shoulder with you.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhi, using Sun Hao's song in reply, answered: "Once I was your subject; now I stand shoulder to shoulder with you.

sentences.zh: 既不勸汝酒，亦不願汝年。」

translations.literal: I will neither urge you to drink, nor wish you long years."
translations.idiomatic: I will neither urge you to drink, nor wish you long years."

sentences.zh: 邕所至嗜食瘡痂，以為味似鰒魚。

translations.literal: Wherever Yong went, he loved to eat scabs, thinking the flavor resembled abalone.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yong went, he loved to eat scabs, thinking the flavor resembled abalone.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣孟靈休，靈休先患灸瘡，瘡痂落牀上，因取食之。

translations.literal: Once he called on Meng Lingxiu. Lingxiu had earlier suffered moxibustion sores; scabs fell onto the bed, and Yong picked them up and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: Once he called on Meng Lingxiu. Lingxiu had earlier suffered moxibustion sores; scabs fell onto the bed, and Yong picked them up and ate them.

sentences.zh: 靈休大驚。

translations.literal: Lingxiu was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxiu was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「性之所嗜。」

translations.literal: He replied: "It is what my nature loves."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "It is what my nature loves."

sentences.zh: 靈休瘡痂未落者，悉褫取以飴邕。

translations.literal: Every scab on Lingxiu that had not yet fallen off, he stripped away entirely to feed Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Every scab on Lingxiu that had not yet fallen off, he stripped away entirely to feed Yong.

sentences.zh: 邕既去，靈休與何勗書曰：「劉邕向顧見噉，遂舉體流血。」

translations.literal: After Yong left, Lingxiu wrote to He Xu: "When Liu Yong turned and saw me being eaten, my whole body bled."
translations.idiomatic: After Yong left, Lingxiu wrote to He Xu: "When Liu Yong turned and saw me being devoured, my whole body bled."

sentences.zh: 南康國吏二百許人，[7]不問有罪無罪，遞互與鞭，鞭瘡痂常以給膳。

translations.literal: About two hundred officials of the Nankang State,[7] regardless of guilt or innocence, were flogged in rotation; the scabs from flogging were regularly supplied for his meals.
translations.idiomatic: About two hundred officials of the Nankang State,[7] regardless of guilt or innocence, were flogged in rotation; the scabs from flogging were regularly supplied for his meals.

sentences.zh: 卒，子肜嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Tong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Tong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，坐刀斫妻，奪爵土，以弟彪紹封。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming, for hacking his wife with a knife he was stripped of rank and fief; his younger brother Biao continued the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming, for hacking his wife with a knife he was stripped of rank and fief; his younger brother Biao continued the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，降為南康縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the title was reduced to Marquis of Nankang County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, the title was reduced to marquis of Nankang County with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 穆之中子式之字延叔，通易好士。

translations.literal: Muzhi's second son Shizhi, courtesy name Yanshu, mastered the Changes and loved scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi's second son Shizhi, courtesy name Yanshu, mastered the Changes and loved scholars.

sentences.zh: 累遷相國中兵參軍，太子中舍人，黃門侍郎，寧朔將軍、宣城淮南二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Central Army Aide of the Chancellor's State, Central Palace Attendant to the Heir, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of both Xuancheng and Huainan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to central army aide of the chancellor's state, central palace attendant to the heir, gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and general who pacifies the north and administrator of both Xuancheng and Huainan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 在任贓貨狼藉，揚州刺史王弘遣從事檢校。

translations.literal: While in office his corrupt goods were scattered everywhere; Wang Hong, Inspector of Yang Province, sent an aide to inspect and verify.
translations.idiomatic: While in office his corrupt goods were scattered everywhere; Wang Hong, inspector of Yang Province, sent an aide to inspect and verify.

sentences.zh: 從事呼攝吏民，欲加辯覆。

translations.literal: The aide summoned and seized officials and commoners, intending to cross-examine them.
translations.idiomatic: The aide summoned and seized officials and commoners, intending to cross-examine them.

sentences.zh: 式之召從事謂曰：「治所還白使君，劉式之於國家粗有微分，偷數百萬錢何有，況不偷邪！

translations.literal: Shizhi summoned the aide and said: "Go back and report to the Inspector: Liu Shizhi has some slight standing with the state — what is stealing a few million cash? Much less not stealing!
translations.idiomatic: Shizhi summoned the aide and said: "Go back and report to the inspector: Liu Shizhi has some slight standing with the state — what is stealing a few million cash? Much less not stealing!

sentences.zh: 吏民及文書不可得。」

translations.literal: The officials, commoners, and documents are not obtainable."
translations.idiomatic: The officials, commoners, and documents are not obtainable."

sentences.zh: 從事還具白弘，弘曰：「劉式之辯如此奔！」

translations.literal: The aide returned and fully reported to Wang Hong. Hong said: "Liu Shizhi's defense is this reckless!"
translations.idiomatic: The aide returned and fully reported to Wang Hong. Hong said: "Liu Shizhi's defense is this reckless!"

sentences.zh: 亦由此得停。

translations.literal: Because of this the investigation was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the investigation was halted.

sentences.zh: 還為太子右率，左衞將軍，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He later served as Right Leader of the Heir's Guard, Left Guard General, and Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as right leader of the heir's guard, left guard general, and administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted the title General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted the title general who punishes the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 從征關、洛有功，封德陽縣五等侯，諡曰恭侯。

translations.literal: For merit in campaigns at Guan and Luo he was enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Marquis of Deyang County, posthumous title Marquis Gong.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in campaigns at Guan and Luo he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank marquis of Deyang County, with the posthumous title Marquis Gong.

sentences.zh: 長子敳，世祖初，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: The eldest son Ai, at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Ai, at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, served as gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 敳弟衍，大明末，以為黃門郎，出為豫章內史。

translations.literal: Ai's younger brother Yan, at the end of the Daming era, was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and sent out as Internal Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Ai's younger brother Yan, at the end of the Daming era, was appointed gentleman of the Yellow Gate and sent out as internal administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 晉安王子勛稱偽號，以為中護軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin'an Zixun proclaimed a false reign title, Yan was made Central Army Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jin'an Zixun proclaimed a false reign title, Yan was made central army guard general.

sentences.zh: 事敗伏誅。

translations.literal: When the affair failed he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair failed he was executed.

sentences.zh: 衍弟瑀字茂琳，少有才氣，為太祖所知。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Maolin, from youth had talent and spirit, and was known to Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Maolin, from youth had talent and spirit, and was known to Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 始興王濬為南徐州，以瑀補別駕從事史，為濬所遇。

translations.literal: When Prince of Shixing Jun was governor of South Xuzhou, Yu was appointed as Attendant Master and Staff Officer and was favored by Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Shixing Jun was governor of South Xuzhou, Yu was appointed as attendant master and staff officer and was favored by Jun.

sentences.zh: 瑀性陵物護前，不欲人居己上。

translations.literal: Yu by nature looked down on others and protected his own precedence; he did not wish anyone to stand above him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu by nature looked down on others and protected his own precedence; he did not wish anyone to stand above him.

sentences.zh: 時濬征北府行參軍吳郡顧邁輕薄而有才能，濬待之甚厚，深言密事，皆與參之。

translations.literal: At the time Jun's Northern Campaign headquarters Staff Officer Gu Mai of Wu commandery was frivolous yet capable; Jun treated him very generously and shared profound secret matters, all consulting with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jun's northern campaign headquarters staff officer Gu Mai of Wu commandery was frivolous yet capable; Jun treated him very generously and shared profound secret matters, consulting with him on all of them.

sentences.zh: 瑀乃折節事邁，深布情款，家內婦女間事，言語所不得至者，莫不倒寫備說。

translations.literal: Yu then humbled himself to serve Mai, laying out deep affection and trust; matters within the household among women, things words could not reach — none were not copied out and fully told.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then humbled himself to serve Mai, laying out deep affection and trust; matters within the household among women, things words could not reach — none were not copied out and fully told.

sentences.zh: 邁以瑀與之款盡，深相感信。

translations.literal: Mai, because Yu's intimacy with him was complete, deeply felt and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Mai, because Yu's intimacy with him was complete, deeply felt and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 濬所言密事，悉以語瑀。

translations.literal: The secret matters Jun spoke of — all were told to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The secret matters Jun spoke of — all were told to Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑀與邁共進射堂下，瑀忽顧左右索單衣幘，邁問其所以，瑀曰：「公以家人待卿，相與言無所隱，而卿於外宣泄，致使人無不知。

translations.literal: Yu and Mai together entered below the archery hall. Yu suddenly turned to his attendants asking for a plain cap and headcloth. Mai asked why. Yu said: "The Prince treats you like family; you speak together hiding nothing — yet you leak it outside, so that no one does not know.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Mai together entered below the archery hall. Yu suddenly turned to his attendants asking for a plain cap and headcloth. Mai asked why. Yu said: "The prince treats you like family; you speak together hiding nothing — yet you leak it outside, so that everyone knows.

sentences.zh: 我是公吏，何得不啟。」

translations.literal: I am the Prince's official — how could I not report it?"
translations.idiomatic: I am the prince's official — how could I not report it?"

sentences.zh: 因而白之。

translations.literal: And so he reported it.
translations.idiomatic: And so he reported it.

sentences.zh: 濬大怒，啟太祖徙邁廣州。

translations.literal: Jun was greatly angered and memorialized Emperor Wu to transfer Mai to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was greatly angered and memorialized Emperor Wu to transfer Mai to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 邁在廣州，值蕭簡為亂，為之盡力，與簡俱死。

translations.literal: Mai was in Guangzhou when Xiao Jian raised rebellion; he exerted himself fully for Jian and died together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Mai was in Guangzhou when Xiao Jian raised rebellion; he exerted himself fully for Jian and died together with him.

sentences.zh: 瑀遷從事中郎，領淮南太守。

translations.literal: Yu was promoted to Staff Officer and concurrently served as Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was promoted to staff officer and concurrently served as administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年，出為寧遠將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia he was sent out as general who pacifies the distant and inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，以為青州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince assassin usurped the throne, Yu was made Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince assassin usurped the throne, Yu was made inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 瑀聞問，即起義遣軍，并送資實於荊州。

translations.literal: When Yu heard the news, he immediately raised righteous troops and dispatched armies, and also sent supplies and goods to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu heard the news, he immediately raised righteous troops and dispatched armies, and also sent supplies and goods to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，召為御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended, Yu was summoned as Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended, Yu was summoned as imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 還至江陵，值南郡王義宣為逆，瑀陳其不可，言甚切至。

translations.literal: Returning to Jiangling, he encountered Prince of Nanjun Yixuan in rebellion; Yu stated it could not be done, his words very urgent and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Jiangling, he encountered Prince of Nanjun Yixuan in rebellion; Yu stated it could not be done, his words very urgent and direct.

sentences.zh: 義宣以為丞相左司馬，俱至梁山。

translations.literal: Yixuan made him Left Staff Master to the Chancellor; together they reached Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan made him left staff master to the chancellor; together they reached Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 瑀猶乘其蜀中船舫，又有義宣故部曲潛於梁山洲外下投官軍。

translations.literal: Yu still rode in his Shu-region boats and ships, and furthermore had Yixuan's former retainers secretly below Liangshan islet defect to the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Yu still rode in his Shu-region boats and ships, and furthermore had Yixuan's former retainers secretly below Liangshan islet defect to the government army.

sentences.zh: [8]除司徒左長史。

translations.literal: [8] He was appointed Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: [8] He was appointed left chief clerk of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 瑀使氣尚人，為憲司甚得志。

translations.literal: Yu swaggered and looked down on others; as censor he was very satisfied with himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yu swaggered and looked down on others; as censor he was very satisfied with himself.

sentences.zh: 彈王僧達云：「廕籍高華，人品宂末。」

translations.literal: He impeached Wang Sengda, saying: "By inherited registry he is high and splendid; in human quality he is coarse and base."
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Wang Sengda, saying: "By inherited registry he is high and splendid; in human quality he is coarse and base."

sentences.zh: 朝士莫不畏其筆端。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen all feared his pen.
translations.idiomatic: Court gentlemen all feared his pen.

sentences.zh: 尋轉右衞將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to right guard general.

sentences.zh: 瑀願為侍中，不得，謂所親曰：「人仕宦不出當入，不入當出，安能長居戶限上。」

translations.literal: Yu wished to become Palace Attendant but did not obtain it. He said to those close to him: "In official service one either goes in or goes out — how can one long remain on the threshold?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu wished to become palace attendant but did not obtain it. He said to those close to him: "In official service one either goes in or goes out — how can one long remain on the threshold?"

sentences.zh: 因求益州。

translations.literal: And so he requested Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: And so he requested Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖知其此意，許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu understood this intent and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu understood this intent and granted it.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，除輔國將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian he was appointed general who assists the state and inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 既行，甚不得意。

translations.literal: Once he set out, he was very discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Once he set out, he was very discontented.

sentences.zh: 至江陵，與顏竣書曰：「朱脩之三世叛兵，一旦居荊州，青油幙下，作謝宣明面見向，使齋師以長刀引吾下席。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiangling, he wrote to Yan Jun: "Zhu Xiuzhi — rebel soldier for three generations — suddenly holds Jing Province. Under the green-oil canopy he receives audiences like Xie Xuanyuan, and had ritual masters with long knives lead me down from my seat.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Jiangling, he wrote to Yan Jun: "Zhu Xiuzhi — rebel soldier for three generations — suddenly holds Jing Province. Under the green-oil canopy he receives audiences like Xie Xuanyuan, and had ritual masters with long knives lead me down from my seat.

sentences.zh: 於吾何有，政恐匈奴輕漢耳。」

translations.literal: What does that have to do with me? I only fear the Xiongnu will look down on Han."
translations.idiomatic: What does that have to do with me? I only fear the Xiongnu will look down on Han."

sentences.zh: 其年，坐奪人妻為妾，免官。

translations.literal: That year, for taking another man's wife as concubine he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: That year, for taking another man's wife as concubine he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，起為東陽太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming he was recalled to serve as Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daming he returned to office as Grand Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷吳興太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Grand Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 侍中何偃嘗案云：「參伍時望。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant He Yan once said in a dossier: "May be ranked among the men of the age."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant He Yan once wrote in a dossier: "He may be counted among the leading men of the age."

sentences.zh: 瑀大怒曰：「我於時望何參伍之有！」

translations.literal: Yu flew into a rage and said: "What place have I among the men of the age!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu flew into a rage and said: "What place have I among the men of the age!"

sentences.zh: 遂與偃絕。

translations.literal: And so he broke with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with Yan entirely.

sentences.zh: 及為吏部尚書，意彌憤憤。

translations.literal: When he became Director of the Ministry of Personnel, his resentment grew still sharper.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became Director of the Ministry of Personnel, his resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 族叔秀之為丹陽尹，瑀又與親故書曰：「吾家黑面阿秀，遂居劉安眾處，[9]朝廷不為多士。」

translations.literal: His clansman uncle Xiuzhi became Intendant of Danyang; Yu again wrote to kinsmen and friends: "Our family's dark-faced Little Xi has come to sit among Liu Anzhong's crowd,[9] and the court is not a gathering of many talents."
translations.idiomatic: When his clansman uncle Xiuzhi became Intendant of Danyang, Yu wrote again to kinsmen and friends: "That dark-faced Little Xi of our house now sits among Liu Anzhong's crowd,[9] as though the court were no assembly of true talent."

sentences.zh: 其年疽發背，何偃亦發背癕，瑀疾已篤，聞偃亡，歡躍叫呼，於是亦卒。

translations.literal: That year a carbuncle broke out on his back; He Yan also developed a back abscess. Yu's illness was already grave; hearing that Yan had died, he exulted and leaped about shouting, and then he too died.
translations.idiomatic: That year a carbuncle erupted on his back. He Yan developed the same affliction. Yu's illness was already grave; when he heard that Yan had died, he leaped for joy and cried out — and then he too died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰剛子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gengzi ("The Forceful").
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Gengzi, "The Forceful."

sentences.zh: 子卷，南徐州別駕。

translations.literal: His son Juan served as Vice Director of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Juan served as Vice Director of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 卷弟藏，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Juan's younger brother Zang was Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Juan's younger brother Zang served as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 穆之少子貞之，中書黃門侍郎，太子右衞率，寧朔將軍、江夏內史。

translations.literal: Muzhi's youngest son Zhenzhi was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate at the Palace Secretariat, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, General Who Pacifies the North, and Interior Minister of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi's youngest son Zhenzhi held the posts of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate at the Palace Secretariat, Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, General Who Pacifies the North, and Interior Minister of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子裒，始興相，以贓貨繫東冶內。

translations.literal: His son Pou was Chancellor of Shixing; for corrupt taking of goods he was imprisoned in the Eastern Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pou served as Chancellor of Shixing; for taking bribes he was imprisoned in the Eastern Workshop.

sentences.zh: 穆之女適濟陽蔡祐，年老貧窮。

translations.literal: Muzhi's daughter was married to Cai You of Jiyang; in old age she was poor and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi's daughter had married Cai You of Jiyang; in her old age she was poor and destitute.

sentences.zh: 世祖以祐子平南參軍孫為始安太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu made You's son Sun, a staff officer of the Army for Pacifying the South, Administrator of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu appointed You's son Sun, a staff officer of the Army for Pacifying the South, Grand Administrator of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 王弘字休元，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Hong, styled Xiuyuan, was a man of Langya Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, courtesy name Xiuyuan, came from Langya commandery, Linyi county.

sentences.zh: 曾祖導，晉丞相。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dao was Chancellor of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dao had served as Chancellor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖洽，中領軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qia was Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qia had served as Central Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 父珣，司徒。

translations.literal: His father Xun was Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun had served as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 弘少好學，以清恬知名，與尚書僕射謝混善。

translations.literal: Hong from youth loved learning and was famed for pure tranquility; he was on good terms with Xie Hun, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Hong loved study and was known for pure, unassuming temperament; he was close to Xie Hun, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，為會稽王司馬道子驃騎參軍主簿。

translations.literal: At weak-crown age he became chief clerk and staff member to Cavalry General Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he served as chief clerk and staff officer to Cavalry General Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 時農務頓息，末役繁興，弘以為宜建屯田，陳之曰：「近面所諮立屯田事，已具簡聖懷。

translations.literal: At the time agricultural work had suddenly ceased and corvée labor proliferated; Hong thought garrison farms should be established and stated: "On our recent audience I discussed establishing garrison farms; the matter has already been set out in brief for the sage mind.
translations.idiomatic: At the time farming had suddenly stalled while corvée levies multiplied; Hong argued that garrison farms should be established and submitted a statement: "In our recent audience I discussed establishing garrison farms, and the matter has already been laid before your sagely mind.

sentences.zh: 南畝事興，時不可失，宜早督田畯，以要歲功。

translations.literal: When work in the southern fields begins, the season cannot be lost; we should quickly supervise the field officers to secure the year's harvest.
translations.idiomatic: When planting in the southern fields begins, the season cannot be missed; field officers should be urged at once to secure the year's harvest.

sentences.zh: 而府資役單刻，[10]控引無所，雖復厲以重勸，肅以嚴威，適足令囹圄充積，而無救於事實也。

translations.literal: Yet the headquarters' labor resources are scant,[10] with nothing to draw upon; even if we press them with heavy incentives and awe them with strict majesty, it would only fill the prisons while doing nothing for the actual problem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the headquarters' labor pool is too thin,[10] with no reserves to draw on; even heavy incentives and stern threats would only fill the prisons without remedying the real shortage.

sentences.zh: 伏見南局諸冶，募吏數百，雖資以廩贍，收入甚微。

translations.literal: I observe that the southern bureau's various smelting works employ several hundred conscript clerks; though they are supplied with grain rations, the revenue taken in is very slight.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the southern bureau's smelting works employ several hundred conscript clerks; though they receive grain rations, the revenue they yield is negligible.

sentences.zh: 愚謂若回以配農，必功利百倍矣。

translations.literal: I venture to suggest that if these men were reassigned to farming, the benefit and profit would be a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: I suggest that if these men were reassigned to farming, the public benefit would increase a hundredfold.

sentences.zh: 然軍器所須，不可都廢，今欲留銅官大冶及都邑小冶各一所，重其功課，一准揚州，州之求取，亦當無乏，餘者罷之，以充東作之要。

translations.literal: Yet military equipment is indispensable and cannot all be abolished; I now propose retaining one major smeltery at Tongguan and one small smeltery in the capital district each, doubling their labor quotas to match Yang Province's standard — the province's requisitions should then suffer no shortage — and abolishing the rest to meet the urgent needs of spring planting.
translations.idiomatic: Military equipment cannot be abandoned entirely; I propose keeping one major smeltery at Tongguan and one small smeltery in the capital, doubling their labor quotas to Yang Province's standard so that provincial requisitions will not fall short, and abolishing the rest to supply the urgent work of spring planting.

sentences.zh: 又欲二局田曹，各立典軍募吏，依冶募比例，并聽取山湖人，此皆無損於私，有益於公者也。

translations.literal: I also propose that the two bureaus' field-office sections each establish recruiting officers for conscript clerks at the same ratio as the smelting works, and that lake-and-mountain people be allowed to join as well — all of this harms no private interest while benefiting the public weal.
translations.idiomatic: I also propose that each of the two bureaus' field offices establish recruiting officers for conscript clerks on the same scale as the smelting works, and that people of the lakes and mountains be allowed to join — all at no cost to private interests and with clear benefit to the public weal.

sentences.zh: 其中亦應疇量，分判番假，及給廩多少，自可一以委之本曹。

translations.literal: Details such as measuring allotments, assigning rotation and leave, and fixing grain rations should all be entrusted entirely to the field office itself.
translations.idiomatic: Questions of measuring allotments, assigning rotations and leave, and setting grain rations should all be left entirely to the field office.

sentences.zh: 親局所統，必當練悉，且近東曹板水曹參軍納之領此任，其人頗有幹能，自足了其事耳。

translations.literal: The bureau directly in charge must be thoroughly familiar with the matter; moreover, the Eastern Bureau's Board of Works and Water Board staff officer Na, recently put in charge of this duty, is quite capable — he alone would suffice for the task.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau in direct charge must know the work thoroughly; moreover, Na, staff officer of the Eastern Bureau's Board of Works and Water Board, recently assigned this duty, is quite capable and would suffice on his own.

sentences.zh: 頃年以來，斯務弛廢，田蕪廩虛，實亦由此。

translations.literal: In recent years this work has lapsed and been abandoned; fields lie fallow and granaries empty — the cause lies truly here.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years this work has been neglected; fields lie fallow and granaries empty — and the cause lies here.

sentences.zh: 弘過蒙飾擢，志輸短効，豈可相與寢默，有懷弗聞邪！

translations.literal: Hong has undeservedly received ornament and promotion, and his will is to offer whatever small service he can — how can we together remain silent and let what weighs on the heart go unspoken!
translations.idiomatic: Hong has undeservedly received favor and promotion, and wishes only to offer whatever small service he can — how can we keep silent together and leave what weighs on the heart unspoken!
