sentences.zh: 至於當否，尊自當裁以遠鑒。

translations.literal: As to whether this is right, my lord will surely judge with far-reaching discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Whether this is right, my lord will surely judge with far-reaching discernment.

sentences.zh: 若所啟謬允者，伏願便以時施行，庶歲有務農之勤，倉有盈廩之實，禮節之興，可以垂拱待也。」

translations.literal: If what I submit is granted, I humbly hope it may be implemented in season, so that in the year there is diligence in farming, in the granaries the fullness of storehouses, and the rise of ritual and order may be awaited with folded hands."
translations.idiomatic: If what I submit is approved, I humbly hope it may be carried out in season, so that the year brings diligence in farming, the granaries fullness, and the flourishing of ritual and order may be awaited with folded hands."

sentences.zh: 道子欲以為黃門侍郎，珣以其年少固辭。

translations.literal: Daozi wished to make him Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, but Xun, because he was young, firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi wished to appoint him Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, but Xun, citing his son's youth, firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 珣頗好積聚，財物布在民間。

translations.literal: Xun greatly loved accumulation; wealth and goods were spread among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had been fond of amassing wealth, with loans scattered far and wide among the people.

sentences.zh: 珣薨，弘悉燔燒券書，一不收責；

translations.literal: When Xun died, Hong burned all bond-deeds and collected nothing owed;
translations.idiomatic: When Xun died, Hong burned every bond and pressed no debtor for repayment;

sentences.zh: 餘舊業悉以委付諸弟。

translations.literal: the rest of the old estate he wholly entrusted to his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: he turned the remainder of the family holdings over entirely to his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 未免喪，後將軍司馬元顯以為諮議參軍，加寧遠將軍，知記室事，固辭不就。

translations.literal: Before he had finished mourning, Rear General Sima Yuansian wished to make him Adviser and add the title General Who Pacifies the Distant, with charge of secretarial affairs; he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Before his mourning was complete, Rear General Sima Yuansian wished to appoint him Adviser with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant and charge of secretarial affairs; Hong firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 道子復以為諮議參軍，加建威將軍，領中兵，又固辭。

translations.literal: Daozi again wished to make him Adviser, add the title General Who Establishes Might, and put him in charge of the central army; again he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi again wished to appoint him Adviser, add the title General Who Establishes Might, and put him in charge of the central army; again he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 時內外多難，在喪者皆不終其哀，唯弘固執得免。

translations.literal: At the time troubles were many within and without; those in mourning could not complete their grief, yet Hong alone held firm and was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was racked by turmoil inside and out, and mourners could scarcely finish their rites — yet Hong alone held firm and was left in peace.

sentences.zh: 桓玄剋京邑，收道子付廷尉，臣吏畏恐，莫敢瞻送。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan took the capital, he handed Daozi over to the Court of Justice; clerks and officers were fearful and dared not look on or escort him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized the capital he delivered Daozi to the Court of Justice; clerks and officers were terrified and dared neither watch nor follow him.

sentences.zh: 弘時尚在喪，獨於道側拜，攀車涕泣，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: Hong was still in mourning yet alone bowed by the roadside, clinging to the carriage and weeping; commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was still in mourning, yet he alone bowed from the roadside, clinging to the carriage in tears — and commentators praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 高祖為鎮軍，召補諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu served as General Who Guards the Army, he summoned Hong to fill the post of Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu served as General Who Guards the Army, he summoned Hong as Adviser.

sentences.zh: 以功封華容縣五等侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Huarong County.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Huarong County.

sentences.zh: 遷琅邪王大司馬從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman in the headquarters of the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 出為寧遠將軍、琅邪內史，尚書吏部郎中，豫章相。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Interior Minister of Langye, Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing, and Chancellor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the Distant and Interior Minister of Langye, also serving as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel in the Masters of Writing and Chancellor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 盧循寇南康諸郡，弘奔尋陽。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun raided the commanderies around Nankang, Hong fled to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun raided the commanderies around Nankang, Hong fled to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖復命為中軍諮議參軍，遷大司馬右長史，轉吳國內史。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu again appointed him Adviser to the Central Army, promoted him to Right Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal, and transferred him to Interior Minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu again appointed him Adviser to the Central Army, then promoted him to Right Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal and transferred him to Interior Minister of Wu.

sentences.zh: 義熙十一年，徵為太尉長史，轉左長史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yixi he was summoned as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant and transferred to Left Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yixi he was summoned as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant and then transferred to Left Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 從北征，前鋒已平洛陽，而未遣九錫，弘銜使還京師，諷旨朝廷。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign the vanguard had already pacified Luoyang, yet the Nine Bestowments had not been sent; Hong, bearing an envoy's charge, returned to the capital to hint at the court.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern campaign the vanguard had already taken Luoyang, but the Nine Bestowments had not yet been granted; Hong returned to the capital on embassy to nudge the court toward that step.

sentences.zh: 時劉穆之掌留任，而旨反從北來，穆之愧懼，發病遂卒。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Muzhi held the duties left behind in the capital, yet the imperial intent came from the north; Muzhi, ashamed and afraid, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi was then in charge at the capital, but the emperor's intent arrived from the north; stricken with shame and fear, Muzhi fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 而高祖還彭城，弘領彭城太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu returned to Pengcheng, Hong concurrently served as Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu returned to Pengcheng, Hong also served as Administrator of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 宋國初建，遷尚書僕射領選，太守如故。

translations.literal: When the state of Song was first established, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in charge of appointments, while retaining his post as administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song state was first established, he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with charge of appointments, while retaining his post as administrator.

sentences.zh: 奏彈謝靈運曰：「臣聞閑厥有家，垂訓大易，作威專戮，致誡周書。

translations.literal: He memorialized to impeach Xie Lingyun, saying: "I have heard that the household must be governed with rectitude — so the Great Change teaches; that wielding authority and killing at will brings warning — so the Book of Zhou admonishes.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted an impeachment of Xie Lingyun, saying: "I have heard that governing the household requires rectitude — so the Great Change teaches; that wielding authority and killing at will brings warning — so the Book of Zhou admonishes.

sentences.zh: 斯典或違，刑茲無赦。

translations.literal: When such canonical norms are violated, punishment must admit no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When such canonical norms are violated, punishment must admit no pardon.

sentences.zh: 世子左衞率康樂縣公謝靈運，力人桂興淫其嬖妾，殺興江涘，棄尸洪流。

translations.literal: Xie Lingyun, Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Duke of Kangle County, had a strongman named Gui Xing violate his favorite concubine; Lingyun killed Xing by the riverbank and cast the corpse into the rushing stream.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Lingyun, Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Duke of Kangle County, had a strongman named Gui Xing violate his favorite concubine; Lingyun killed Xing by the riverbank and threw the body into the torrent.

sentences.zh: 事發京畿，播聞遐邇。

translations.literal: The affair broke out in the capital region and spread in fame to far and near.
translations.idiomatic: The affair broke out in the capital region and was known far and wide.

sentences.zh: 宜加重劾，肅正朝風。

translations.literal: He should receive a heavier impeachment to rectify the court's wind.
translations.idiomatic: He should be impeached with full severity to rectify the tone of the court.

sentences.zh: 案世子左衞率康樂縣公謝靈運過蒙恩奬，頻叨榮授，聞禮知禁，為日已久。

translations.literal: I find that Xie Lingyun, Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Duke of Kangle County, has undeservedly received the court's grace and has repeatedly been granted honorable posts; he has understood ritual and known prohibition for many days.
translations.idiomatic: I find that Xie Lingyun, Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Duke of Kangle County, has undeservedly received the court's grace and has repeatedly been granted honorable posts; he has long understood ritual and known what is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 而不能防閑閫闈，致茲紛穢，罔顧憲軌，忿殺自由。

translations.literal: Yet he could not guard the inner quarters, and so this sordid affair arose; heedless of the law's track, he killed in free rage.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not guard his inner household, and so this sordid affair arose; heedless of the law, he killed in unchecked rage.

sentences.zh: 此而勿治，典刑將替。

translations.literal: If this is not punished, canonical punishment will fall away.
translations.idiomatic: If this goes unpunished, the canonical punishments will fall into disuse.

sentences.zh: 請以見事免靈運所居官，上臺削爵土，收付大理治罪。

translations.literal: I request that, on the basis of this matter, Lingyun be removed from his post, that the upper offices strip his rank and fief, and that he be handed over to the Grand Judge for punishment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: I request that, on the basis of this matter, Lingyun be removed from office, that the upper offices strip his rank and fief, and that he be handed over to the Grand Judge for punishment according to law.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞都亭侯王准之，[11]顯居要任，邦之司直，風聲噂𠴲，曾不彈舉。

translations.literal: Wang Zhunzhi, Imperial Censor and Marquis of Duting,[11] prominently holds a crucial post, the state's uprightness; rumors and gossip spread, yet he never impeached or reported.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhunzhi, Imperial Censor and Marquis of Duting,[11] holds a crucial post as the state's uprightness; rumors spread far and wide, yet he never impeached or reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 若知而弗糾，則情法斯撓；

translations.literal: If he knew and did not investigate, then sentiment and law alike are bent;
translations.idiomatic: If he knew and failed to investigate, then both sentiment and law are bent;

sentences.zh: 如其不知，則尸昧已甚。

translations.literal: if he truly did not know, then his corpse-like oblivion is already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: if he truly did not know, then his oblivious dereliction is already extreme.

sentences.zh: 豈可復預班清階，式是國憲。

translations.literal: How can he again tread the pure ranks and embody the state's law?
translations.idiomatic: How can he again stand in the pure ranks and embody the state's law?

sentences.zh: 請免所居官，以侯還散輩中。

translations.literal: I request that he be removed from his post and returned as marquis to the ranks of inactive nobles.
translations.idiomatic: I request that he be removed from office and returned as marquis to the ranks of inactive nobles.

sentences.zh: 內臺舊體，不得用風聲舉彈，此事彰赫，曝之朝野，執憲蔑聞，羣司循舊，國典既頹，所虧者重。

translations.literal: The old rule of the inner censorate does not permit impeachment on the basis of hearsay; but this affair blazes so brightly that, exposed to court and realm, the law-enforcer has never heard — yet all offices follow the old ways, and the state norm is already in decay; the loss is grave.
translations.idiomatic: The old rule of the inner censorate does not permit impeachment on hearsay alone; yet this affair blazes so brightly, exposed to court and realm, while the law-enforcer claims never to have heard — all offices follow the old ways, and the state norm is already in decay; the loss is grave.

sentences.zh: 臣弘忝承人乏，位副朝端，若復謹守常科，則終莫之糾正。

translations.literal: Your subject Hong undeservedly bears the human shortfall, with rank second to the court's summit; if I again strictly hold to ordinary statutes, in the end nothing would be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Hong undeservedly fills a post no one else could fill, with rank second only to the summit of court; if I again strictly hold to ordinary statutes, in the end nothing would be corrected.

sentences.zh: 所以不敢拱默，自同秉彝。

translations.literal: Therefore I dare not fold my hands in silence and make myself one who holds the constant law.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I dare not fold my hands in silence and make myself one who merely upholds the letter of the law.

sentences.zh: 違舊之愆，伏須准裁。」

translations.literal: The offense of violating the old rule — I humbly await judgment and decision.
translations.idiomatic: The offense of violating the old rule — I humbly await your judgment and decision.

sentences.zh: 高祖令曰：「靈運免官而已，餘如奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered: "Lingyun is merely removed from office; the rest as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered: "Strip Lingyun of office only; the rest as memorialized.

sentences.zh: 端右肅正風軌，誠副所期，豈拘常儀。

translations.literal: The right hand of government rectifies the wind of governance — truly matching what was hoped; how could one be bound by ordinary ritual?
translations.idiomatic: You at the right hand of government have set the tone straight — truly matching what was hoped; how could one be bound by ordinary ritual?

sentences.zh: 自今為永制。」

translations.literal: From this day let it be the permanent rule."
translations.idiomatic: Let this stand as permanent practice from this day forward."

sentences.zh: 高祖因宴集，謂羣公曰：「我布衣，始望不至此。」

translations.literal: At a banquet Emperor Gaozu said to the assembled lords: "I began as a common cloth-clad man and never expected to reach this point."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Emperor Gaozu said to the assembled lords: "I began as a man in plain cloth and never expected to reach this height."

sentences.zh: 傅亮之徒並撰辭欲盛稱功德。

translations.literal: Fu Liang and his fellows all drafted words wishing to lavishly praise his merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang and his fellows all drafted words wishing to lavishly praise his merit and virtue.

sentences.zh: 弘率爾對曰：「此所謂天命，求之不可得，推之不可去。」

translations.literal: Hong answered offhand: "This is what is called the Mandate of Heaven — sought, it cannot be obtained; pushed away, it cannot be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Hong answered without premeditation: "This is what men call the Mandate of Heaven — sought, it cannot be obtained; pushed away, it cannot be removed."

sentences.zh: 時人稱其簡舉。

translations.literal: People of the time praised his brevity and aptness.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time praised his brevity and aptness.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年，徐羨之等謀廢立，召弘入朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingping under the deposed young emperor, Xu Xianzhi and his fellows plotted deposition and enthronement and summoned Hong to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingping under the deposed young emperor, Xu Xianzhi and his fellows plotted to depose and enthrone and summoned Hong to court.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，以定策安社稷，進位司空，封建安郡公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended, for settling the strategy and securing the altars of soil and grain he was promoted to Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Duke of Jian'an Commandery with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended, for helping settle the strategy and secure the realm he was promoted to Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Duke of Jian'an Commandery with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 上表固辭曰：「臣聞趙武稱隨會夫子之家事治，言於晉國無隱情。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial firmly declining: "I have heard that Duke Wu of Zhao praised Suí Huì's household affairs as well governed, saying to the state of Jin there was no concealment.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial firmly declining: "I have heard that Duke Wu of Zhao praised Suí Huì's household as well governed, saying that to the state of Jin there was no concealment.

sentences.zh: 臣千載幸會，謬荷榮遇，雖以智能虛薄，政績蔑聞，而言無隱情，竊所庶幾。

translations.literal: Your subject, at this thousand-year felicitous meeting, has undeservedly received glory and favor; though my intelligence is hollow and thin and my administrative merit has never been heard of, to speak without concealment is what I privately aspire to.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, at this once-in-a-thousand-years meeting of fortune, has undeservedly received glory and favor; though my intelligence is hollow and thin and my administrative merit has never been heard of, to speak without concealment is what I privately aspire to.

sentences.zh: 向令天啟其心，預定大策，而名編司勳，功不見紀，固將請不賞之罪，懸龍蛇之書，豈當稽違成命，苟修小節。

translations.literal: If Heaven had opened my heart and I had participated in settling the great strategy, yet my name was entered in the merit rolls while my service went unrecorded, I would surely request the punishment of refusing reward and hang up the writ of dragon and snake — how could I delay contrary to the settled command and scrupulously polish small proprieties?
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven had opened my heart and I had shared in settling the great strategy, yet my name was entered in the merit rolls while my service went unrecorded, I would surely request the punishment of refusing reward and hang up the writ of dragon and snake — how could I delay contrary to the settled command and scrupulously polish small proprieties?

sentences.zh: 但無功勤，暴之四海，進闕君子勞心之謀，退微小人勞力之効，而聖朝僭賞於上，愚臣苟忝於下，則為厚誣當時，永貽口實。

translations.literal: But having no meritorious toil, to display this to the four seas — in advance I lack the gentleman's plan of laboring in mind, and in retreat I lack the small man's effect of laboring in strength; yet the sacred court extravagantly rewards from above while this foolish subject undeservedly disgraces from below — then we thickly deceive the age and forever bequeath a matter for mockery.
translations.idiomatic: But having no meritorious toil, to display this to the four seas — in advance I lack the gentleman's plan of laboring in mind, and in retreat I lack the small man's effect of laboring in strength; yet the sacred court extravagantly rewards from above while this foolish subject undeservedly disgraces from below — then we thickly deceive the age and forever bequeath a matter for mockery.

sentences.zh: 竊財之誚，比此為輕，惟塵盛猷，虧玷為大。

translations.literal: The reproach of embezzling wealth is lighter by comparison; only the dust on the grand design — the stain and blemish is great.
translations.idiomatic: The reproach of embezzling wealth is lighter by comparison; only the dust on the grand design — the stain and blemish is great.

sentences.zh: 微躬所惜，一朝亦盡，非唯仰塵國紀，實亦俯畏友朋。

translations.literal: What my insignificant person treasures would in one morning likewise be exhausted — not only upward would I bear the dust of the state norm, but downward I would also bow in fear before friends.
translations.idiomatic: What my insignificant person treasures would in one morning likewise be exhausted — not only upward would I bear the dust of the state norm, but downward I would also bow in fear before friends.

sentences.zh: 憂心彌疹，胡顏靡託。

translations.literal: Anxious sorrow grows ever worse; what face remains to lean on?
translations.idiomatic: Anxious sorrow grows ever worse; what face remains to show?

sentences.zh: 且凡人之交，尚申知己，況在明主，可用理干。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the dealings of ordinary men, one still expresses oneself to an intimate — how much more under an enlightened lord may one appeal to reason?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the dealings of ordinary men one still speaks plainly to an intimate — how much more under an enlightened lord may one appeal to reason?

sentences.zh: 所以敢遂愚狷，守之以死。」

translations.literal: Therefore I dare persist in my foolish stubbornness and hold to this unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I dare persist in my stubborn refusal and hold to this unto death.

sentences.zh: 乃見許。

translations.literal: Thereupon his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 加使持節、侍中，改監為都督，進號車騎大將軍，開府、刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was further given the insignia of envoy and made Palace Attendant; his post as inspector was changed to military commissioner; his title was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry; his grand headquarters and provincial post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted the insignia of envoy and made Palace Attendant; his post as inspector was changed to military commissioner; his title was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry; his grand headquarters and provincial post remained as before.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之等以廢弒之罪將見誅，弘既非首謀，弟曇首又為上所親委，事將發，密使報弘。

translations.literal: When Xu Xianzhi and his fellows were about to be executed for the crimes of deposition and regicide, Hong had not been the chief plotter, and his younger brother Tanshou was also trusted and entrusted by the emperor; as the affair was about to break, they secretly sent word to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Xianzhi and his fellows were about to be executed for deposing and murdering the emperor, Hong had not been the chief plotter, and his younger brother Tanshou was also trusted by the throne; as the affair was about to break, they secretly sent word to Hong.

sentences.zh: 羨之等誅，徵弘為侍中、司徒、揚州刺史，錄尚書。

translations.literal: After Xu Xianzhi and his fellows were executed, Hong was summoned as Palace Attendant, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Yang Province, with charge of the chief records of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Xianzhi and his fellows were executed, Hong was summoned as Palace Attendant, Minister of Education, and Inspector of Yang Province, with charge of the chief records of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 給班劍三十人。

translations.literal: He was granted thirty ceremonial halberds.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted thirty ceremonial halberds.

sentences.zh: 上西征謝晦，弘與驃騎彭城王義康居守，入住中書下省，引隊仗出入。

translations.literal: When the emperor marched west against Xie Hui, Hong and Cavalry General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang remained to guard the capital, taking up residence in the lower offices of the Palace Secretariat, and entered and left with an armed escort.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched west against Xie Hui, Hong and Cavalry General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang remained to guard the capital, taking up residence in the lower offices of the Palace Secretariat and entering and leaving with an armed escort.

sentences.zh: 司徒府權置參軍。

translations.literal: Staff officers were provisionally appointed in the Minister of Education's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officers were provisionally appointed in the Minister of Education's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 五年春，大旱，弘引咎遜位，曰：「臣聞三才雖殊，其致則一。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, during a great drought, Hong took blame upon himself and yielded his post, saying: "I have heard that though the Three Powers differ, their attainment is one.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, during a great drought, Hong took blame upon himself and yielded his post, saying: "I have heard that though Heaven, Earth, and Man differ, their attainment is one.

sentences.zh: 故世道休明，五福攸應；

translations.literal: Thus when the age's way is flourishing and bright, the Five Blessings respond accordingly;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the age's way is flourishing and bright, the Five Blessings respond in kind;

sentences.zh: 政有失德，咎徵必顯。

translations.literal: When government loses virtue, omens of blame are sure to appear.
translations.idiomatic: When government loses virtue, signs of blame are sure to manifest.

sentences.zh: 臣抑又聞之，台輔之職，論道讚契，上佐人主，燮理陰陽。

translations.literal: Your subject further has heard that the duty of the chief ministers is to discourse on the Way and harmonize in accord, to assist the ruler above, and to harmonize yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the chief ministers' duty is to expound the Way and maintain harmony with the sovereign, to assist the ruler from above, and to harmonize yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 位以德授，則和氣淳穆；

translations.literal: When office is granted by virtue, then harmonious qi is pure and solemn;
translations.idiomatic: When office is granted on the basis of virtue, harmonious qi becomes pure and solemn;

sentences.zh: 寇竊非據，則讁見于天。

translations.literal: When bandits steal what is not their rightful place, then reproach appears in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When unworthy men usurp posts they do not deserve, reproach appears in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 是以陳平有辭，不濫主者之局；

translations.literal: Thus Chen Ping had reasons and did not improperly fill the ruler's role;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Chen Ping had cause to decline and did not improperly assume the ruler's position;

sentences.zh: 邴吉停駕，大懼牛喘之由。

translations.literal: Bing Ji stopped his carriage, greatly fearing the cause of the ox's panting.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji halted his carriage, deeply alarmed at what the panting ox might signify.

sentences.zh: 斯固有國之所同，天人之遠旨。

translations.literal: This is indeed what all states share in common — the far-reaching purport of Heaven and Man.
translations.idiomatic: This is indeed what all states hold in common — the far-reaching purpose that links Heaven and humanity.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖哲御世，光隆中興，[12]宜休徵表祥，醴泉毖涌。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, sage and wise in governing the age, gloriously elevating the restoration, [12] ought to have auspicious signs appear as blessings, and sweet springs gush abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is sage and wise in governing the age, gloriously bringing the restoration to fruition, [12] and ought to see auspicious signs and sweet springs gushing forth abundantly.

sentences.zh: 而頃陰陽隔并，亢旱成災，秋無嚴霜，冬無積雪，疾厲之氣，彌歷四時。

translations.literal: Yet recently yin and yang are separated and out of alignment, severe drought becomes disaster, autumn has no hard frost, winter has no accumulated snow, and pestilential qi fills all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recently yin and yang have fallen out of balance, severe drought has brought disaster, autumn has known no hard frost, winter no accumulated snow, and pestilence has spread through all four seasons.

sentences.zh: 此豈非任失其人，覆餗之咎。

translations.literal: Is this not the fault of appointing the wrong man and the calamity of the overturned soup kettle?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not the fault of putting the wrong man in office — the calamity of the overturned soup kettle?

sentences.zh: 臣以庸短，自輩凡流，謬逢嘉運，叨恩在昔。

translations.literal: Your subject, by mediocrity and shortcoming, ranks himself among the common stream, wrongly encountering a felicitous age and undeservedly receiving grace in times past.
translations.idiomatic: I am mediocre and limited, no more than one of the common run, who by sheer fortune encountered a blessed age and undeservedly received favor in years past.

sentences.zh: 陛下忘其不腆，又重之以今任。

translations.literal: Your Majesty forgot my unworthiness and further burdened me with the present appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty overlooked my unworthiness and further burdened me with my present appointment.

sentences.zh: 正位槐鼎，統理神州，珥貂衣袞，總錄朝端，內外要重，頓萃微躬，窮極寵貴，人臣莫比。

translations.literal: Holding rightful place among the cypress and ding, governing the heartland, wearing fur on the cap and the ceremonial robe, overseeing all affairs at court, important posts within and without all at once gathered upon my insignificant person — favor and rank at the utmost, no minister comparable.
translations.idiomatic: I hold the highest ministerial posts, govern the heartland, wear the fur of office and the ceremonial robe, and oversee all affairs at court — every weighty post within and without has been heaped upon my insignificant person; favor and rank could go no higher, and no minister compares.

sentences.zh: 令德居之，猶或難稱，矧伊陋昧，何以克任。

translations.literal: Even one of outstanding virtue occupying it might still find it hard to answer to, how much more this base and dull one — how could he fulfill the charge?
translations.idiomatic: Even a man of outstanding virtue might scarcely fill such a role; how much less could someone as base and dull as I hope to bear the charge?

sentences.zh: 此之易了，不俟明識。

translations.literal: This is easy to see, and needs no wait for keen insight.
translations.idiomatic: This is easy enough to see and requires no keen insight to understand.

sentences.zh: 但受命之始，屬值時艱，六戎親戒，憂及社稷，誠是臣下致節忘身之時，當有何心，塵撓聖聽。

translations.literal: Yet at the beginning of receiving my charge, the times were hard — the Six Rong personally threatening, worry reaching the altars of soil and grain — truly a time for subjects to give full loyalty and forget their persons; what heart could I have to cloud and trouble the sacred ear?
translations.idiomatic: But when I first took office, the times were desperate — the barbarians threatening at the borders, the altars of soil and grain in peril — and it was truly a moment for subjects to devote themselves utterly. What heart could I have had to trouble Your Majesty's ear?

sentences.zh: 所以僶俛從事，循牆馳驅，志在宣力，慮不及遠。

translations.literal: Therefore I exerted myself and bowed to the task, hugging the wall and racing onward, my will set on exerting effort, my thought not reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I applied myself diligently, clinging to the wall and pressing forward, intent only on doing what I could, with no thought for the long term.

sentences.zh: 既鯨鯢折首，西夏底定，便宜訴其本懷，避賢謝拙。

translations.literal: Once the whales and crocodiles had broken heads and Western Xia was settled, I ought properly to express my true heart and yield to the worthy while declining my inadequacy.
translations.idiomatic: Once the great enemies had been broken and the western regions pacified, I ought to have expressed my true feelings and yielded to better men while confessing my inadequacy.

sentences.zh: 而常人偷安，日甘一日，實亦仰佩天眷，未能自已。

translations.literal: Yet as an ordinary man I sought ease and day by day found it sweet — in truth also looking up in awe at Heaven's favor, unable to restrain myself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet like any ordinary man I sought ease and grew content day by day — in truth also awed by Heaven's favor upon me, and unable to stop myself.

sentences.zh: 荏苒推遷，忽及三載。

translations.literal: Time passed in flowing shifts, and suddenly three years had elapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Time flowed on, and before I knew it three years had passed.

sentences.zh: 遂令負乘之釁，彰著幽明；

translations.literal: Thereby causing the omen of the unfit rider to appear clearly in darkness and light;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the omen of the unfit rider has become plain to both the living and the dead;

sentences.zh: 愆伏之災，患纏氓庶。

translations.literal: Disasters of fault and hidden sin afflict and entangle the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Disasters born of hidden faults now afflict the common people.

sentences.zh: 上缺皇朝緝熙之美，下增官謗覆折之災。

translations.literal: Above it lacks the brightness of the royal court's glorious governance; below it increases officials' slander and the disaster of overturning and breaking.
translations.idiomatic: Above, it blemishes the radiance of the imperial court's governance; below, it increases official scandal and the calamity of ruin.

sentences.zh: 伏念惶赧，五情飛散，雖曰厚顏，何以寧處。

translations.literal: Prostrate I reflect, fearful and ashamed, the five feelings scattered in flight — though one may speak of thick face, how can one rest in peace?
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate in reflection, I am fearful and ashamed, my every feeling scattered — shameless though I may be called, how can I rest at ease?

sentences.zh: 不遠而復，大易攸稱，小懲大戒，細人之福。

translations.literal: Not going far before returning — the Great Changes thus praises it; small punishment, great warning — the petty man's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Not going far before turning back — this the Book of Changes praises; a small punishment can serve as a great warning, and that is the petty man's blessing.

sentences.zh: 近復之美，非所敢觖，懲戒之幸，竊懷庶幾。

translations.literal: The beauty of soon returning — I dare not aspire to it; the fortune of warning and correction — I privately hope for something of it.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not hope for the glory of a swift return; I can only pray for the fortune of receiving correction.

sentences.zh: 今履端惟始，朝慶禮畢，輒還私門，思愆家巷，庶微塞天譴，少弭謗讟。

translations.literal: Now at the year's beginning, when the court celebration rites are finished, I would at once return to my private gate, to reflect on faults in my home lane, hoping in some small measure to block Heaven's reprimand and slightly quell slander and reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Now at the year's beginning, once the court celebration is finished, I would return to my private home, there to reflect on my faults, hoping in some small measure to avert Heaven's reprimand and ease the slander against me.

sentences.zh: 伏願鑑其所守，即而許之。

translations.literal: Prostrate I wish Your Majesty to examine what I uphold and immediately grant it.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will discern my sincerity and grant my request.

sentences.zh: 臨啟愧塞，不自宣盡。」

translations.literal: On presenting this memorial I am ashamed and blocked, unable to express it fully."
translations.idiomatic: As I present this memorial, shame overwhelms me and I cannot say all I feel."

sentences.zh: 先是彭城王義康為荊州刺史，鎮江陵。

translations.literal: Earlier Prince of Pengcheng Yikang had been Inspector of Jing Province, stationed at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince of Pengcheng Yikang had served as Inspector of Jing Province, stationed at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 平陸令河南成粲與弘書曰：「僕聞軌物設教，必隨時制宜；

translations.literal: Pinglu Magistrate Cheng Can of Henan wrote to Hong saying: "I have heard that regulating things and establishing instruction must follow the times and suit circumstances;
translations.idiomatic: Pinglu Magistrate Cheng Can of Henan wrote to Hong, saying: "I have heard that to regulate affairs and establish instruction one must adapt to the times and suit circumstances;

sentences.zh: 世代盈虛，亦與之消息。

translations.literal: Generations wax and wane, and likewise accord with it in ebb and flow.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasties rise and fall, and policy must rise and fall with them.

sentences.zh: 夫勢之所處，非親不居。

translations.literal: As for positions of power where one is situated, none but the close kin should occupy them.
translations.idiomatic: Positions of power should be held by none but those closest to the throne.

sentences.zh: 是以周之宗盟，異姓為後。

translations.literal: Thus in Zhou's enfeoffment alliance, those of different surnames came after.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the Zhou enfeoffment system, those of different surnames ranked below.

sentences.zh: 權軸之要，任歸二南，斯前代之明謨，當今之顯轍。

translations.literal: The crucial pivot of power — the charge returns to the Two Nan; this is the enlightened design of former ages and the plain path of the present day.
translations.idiomatic: The pivot of power should rest with the royal kin — this was the enlightened design of former ages and is the plain path for our own day.

sentences.zh: 明公位極台鼎，四海具瞻，劬勞夙夜，義同吐握。

translations.literal: My lord has reached the pinnacle of chief ministership, the four seas all look to you, toiling early and late — your righteousness equals spitting in the palm and clasping hands.
translations.idiomatic: My lord stands at the pinnacle of government, the whole realm looks to you, toiling from dawn to dusk with a devotion equal to Duke Zhou's "spitting in his palm and clasping hands."

sentences.zh: 而總錄百揆，兼牧畿甸，功實盛大，莫之與儔。

translations.literal: Yet overseeing all the hundred affairs and concurrently governing the capital domain — your merit is truly grand, none to match with you.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you oversee all affairs of state and govern the capital domain as well — your power is truly immense, and none can compare.

sentences.zh: 天道福謙，宜存挹損。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way blesses humility; you ought to preserve modest restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way blesses humility; you ought to preserve modest restraint.

sentences.zh: 驃騎彭城王道德昭備，上之懿弟，宗本歸源，所應推先，〔宜入秉朝政，翊贊皇猷。

translations.literal: Cavalry General Prince of Pengcheng — his virtue and conduct fully evident, the emperor's honored younger brother, the source to which the clan returns — should be put first, [ought to enter and hold court governance, assist and support the imperial design.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry General the Prince of Pengcheng possesses shining virtue, is the emperor's honored younger brother and the root of the royal house — he should be placed first, [and ought to take charge of court governance and support the imperial design.

sentences.zh: 竟陵、衡陽春秋已長，又〕宜出據列蕃，齊光魯、衞。

translations.literal: Jingling and Hengyang — their years already grown — again] ought to go out and hold the various domains, sharing glory with Lu and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Jingling and Hengyang have come of age as well,] and ought to take up command of the various domains, sharing in the glory of the ancient marquisates of Lu and Wei.

sentences.zh: [13]明公高枕論道，燮理陰陽，則天下和平，災害不作，福慶與大宋升降，享年與松、喬齊久，名垂萬代，豈不美歟！」

translations.literal: [13] My lord, reclining high to discourse on the Way and harmonize yin and yang — then all under Heaven is at peace, disasters do not arise, blessing and felicity rise and fall with Great Song, years enjoyed equal to Song and Qiao's long span, name handed down ten thousand generations — is it not beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: [13] My lord could then rest at ease, expounding the Way and harmonizing yin and yang — all under Heaven would be at peace, disasters would cease, your blessings would rise and fall with the Song dynasty, your years would match those of the immortals Song and Qiao, and your name would endure for ten thousand generations — would that not be splendid!

sentences.zh: 弘本有退志，挾粲言，由是固自陳請，乃降為衞將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Hong originally had the will to withdraw; taking Cheng Can's words, thereupon he firmly memorialized his request and was then reduced to General of the Guard, with grand headquarters and ceremonials equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had already wished to retire; bolstered by Cheng Can's letter, he pressed his request all the more firmly and was reduced to General of the Guard with grand headquarters and ceremonials equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 六年，弘又上表曰：「臣聞異姓為後，宗周之明義；

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Hong again submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that different surnames come after — the enlightened principle of honoring Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Hong again submitted a memorial, saying: "I have heard that those of different surnames rank below — the enlightened principle by which the Zhou honored their royal house;

sentences.zh: 親不在外，有國之所先。

translations.literal: Relatives not placed outside — what a state puts first.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping kin close and outsiders at arm's length — this is what every state puts first.

sentences.zh: 故魯長滕君，春秋所美，楚出棄疾，前史垂誡。

translations.literal: Thus the Elder Lord of Teng in Lu was praised by the Spring and Autumn, while Chu sent out Qi Ji — the former histories hand down a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Elder Lord of Teng in Lu was praised in the Spring and Autumn Annals, while Chu sent Qi Ji into exile — the earlier histories preserve both the model and the warning.

sentences.zh: 矧乃茂親明德，道光一時，述職侯甸，朝政弗及，而以庶族庸陋浮華之臣，超踰先典，居中贊契，豈所以憲章古式，緝熙治道？

translations.literal: How much more when an illustrious kinsman of bright virtue, his Way shining for an age, performs duty in the marquisate domains yet cannot reach court governance — yet a vulgar, base, flashy minister of common clan surpasses the earlier canon, sits at the center harmonizing with the ruler — how is this to be the model of ancient forms and the bright governance of the Way?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when an illustrious prince of shining virtue, the light of his age, serves in the marquisate domains yet cannot attend to court governance — while a vulgar, flashy minister of common birth surpasses the precedents of old and sits at the center harmonizing with the throne: how can this be the way to follow ancient models and achieve radiant governance?

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍臣義康，徽猷淵邈，明德彌劭，敷政江漢，化被荊南，搢紳屬情，想樂當務，周旦之寄，不謀同詞，分陝雖重，比此為輕。

translations.literal: Cavalry General your subject Yikang — his fine design profound and far-reaching, bright virtue ever strong, spreading governance over the Jiang and Han, transformation covering southern Jing — gentry and officials attach their hearts, eager with joy for the proper task; the trust of Zhou Gong — without counsel they speak as one; though dividing Shaan was weighty, compared with this it is light.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry General Yikang possesses far-reaching wisdom and ever-growing virtue; he has spread good governance across the Jiang and Han, and his influence has reached all of southern Jing. Officials and gentry look to him with affection and eagerness, and all agree he is fit to bear the trust that Zhou Gong once bore. Though the division of governance at Shaan was weighty, it was lighter than this charge.

sentences.zh: 臣實空闇，階恩踰越，俯積素餐，仰玷盛化，公私二三，無一而可。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly empty and dark, ascending through grace beyond his measure, bowing down accumulating white rice, looking up tarnishing glorious transformation — in public and private two or three things, not one acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: I am truly empty and obtuse, raised beyond my deserts through your grace; I have eaten my salary without earning it and tarnished your glorious rule — in public and private alike I find nothing in myself worth defending.

sentences.zh: 昔孫叔未進，優孟見弞；

translations.literal: Formerly when Sun Shu had not yet advanced, You Meng was seen wiping tears;
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Shu had not yet risen to office, You Meng wept for the state;

sentences.zh: 展季在下，臧文貽譏。

translations.literal: Zhan Ji below, Zang Wen brought mockery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan Ji remained in a low post, Zang Wen was mocked for it.

sentences.zh: 況道隆地昵，義兼前禮。

translations.literal: How much more when the Way is lofty and the ground is close — the principle combines the former rites.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when virtue is eminent and kinship is close — the principle here combines the rites of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臣於古人，無能為役，負乘竊位，萬物謂何，雖曰厚顏，胡寧以處。

translations.literal: Your subject before the ancients can serve as nothing; unfit rider usurping place — what would all things say? Though one speaks of thick face, how could one dwell?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the ancients I am fit for nothing; I am an unfit rider clinging to my post — what would the world say of me? Shameless though I may be called, how can I remain?

sentences.zh: 斯亡之懼，實疚其心。

translations.literal: This fear of ruin truly pains his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The fear of disaster this inspires truly afflicts my heart.

sentences.zh: 乞解州錄，以允民望。

translations.literal: I beg to be released from the provincial charge and chief records, to fulfill the people's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be relieved of my provincial post and charge over the chief records, to satisfy the people's expectation.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下遠存至公，近鑑丹款，俯順朝野，改授親賢。

translations.literal: Prostrate I wish Your Majesty to keep far-reaching impartiality, examine my red sincerity near at hand, bow to follow court and countryside, and change the appointment to a kinsman of worth.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will look to impartiality above all, discern the sincerity of my heart, follow the wishes of court and countryside, and transfer this appointment to a worthy kinsman.

sentences.zh: 豈唯下臣，獲免大戾，凡厥眾隸，孰不慶幸。

translations.literal: Would it not only be your subject below who escapes great guilt — all the multitude of officials, who would not rejoice?
translations.idiomatic: Would this not spare your humble servant alone from great blame — would not every official under Heaven rejoice?

sentences.zh: 若天眷罔已，脫復遲回，請出臣表，逮聞外內，朝議輿誦，或有可擇。」

translations.literal: If Heaven's favor does not cease and you again delay, please publish my memorial, reach hearing within and without, court discussion and public recitation — perhaps something may be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's favor will not release me and Your Majesty still hesitates, please publish my memorial and make it known throughout the realm, so that court and public debate may yield something worth choosing.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「省表，遠擬隆周經國之體，近述大易卑牧之志，三復沖旨，良用憮然。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Having examined the memorial — far drawing on the body of governing the state in flourishing Zhou, near expounding the humble shepherd's will in the Great Changes — thrice returning to its modest purport, truly I am stirred and unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Having read your memorial — which draws from afar on the statecraft of flourishing Zhou and expounds from near the humble shepherd's intent in the Book of Changes — I have read its modest message again and again and am deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 公體道淵虛，明識經遠，毗翼艱難，勳猷光茂，俾朕獲辰居垂拱，司契委成。

translations.literal: My lord's body embraces the Way, profound and empty; bright knowledge extends far; aiding wings in hardship, meritorious design bright and luxuriant — enabling me to obtain the starry seat in repose with folded hands, the tally of covenant entrusted and accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: My lord embodies the Way with profound clarity and far-reaching wisdom; you have supported me through hardship, and your meritorious service shines bright — you have enabled me to sit at ease upon the throne while entrusting you with the seal of governance.

sentences.zh: 豈容高遜總錄，固辭神州，使成務有虧，以重朕之不德邪！

translations.literal: How can one allow lofty yielding of overall charge, firmly declining the heartland, causing established tasks to suffer loss and thereby weighting my lack of virtue!
translations.idiomatic: How can I permit you to yield your overall charge and firmly refuse the heartland, letting great affairs suffer and thereby compounding my own lack of virtue!

sentences.zh: 深存體國，所望夤亮。

translations.literal: Deeply preserve care for the state — this is what I hope and entrust to your bright assistance.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly hope you will continue to care for the state and rely on your loyal assistance.

sentences.zh: 驃騎親賢之寄，地均旦、奭，還入內輔，參讚機務，輒敬從所執。」

translations.literal: The Cavalry General's trust as close kinsman — his ground equal to Dan and Shi — return within as inner assistant, participate and assist in critical affairs; I respectfully follow what you hold to.
translations.idiomatic: The trust placed in the Cavalry General as a close kinsman equals that once placed in the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao; let him return within as inner counsellor and take part in critical affairs. I respectfully defer to your wish in this.

sentences.zh: 義康由是代弘為司徒，與之分錄。

translations.literal: Yikang thereby replaced Hong as Minister of Education and shared the chief records with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang thereupon replaced Hong as Minister of Education, and the two divided the chief records between them.

sentences.zh: 弘又表曰：「近冒表聞，披陳愚管，實冀天鑒，體其至誠。

translations.literal: Hong again memorialized saying: "Recently I presumed to submit a memorial, laying bare my foolish views, truly hoping Heaven's discernment would embody my utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Hong again submitted a memorial, saying: "I recently presumed to lay my views before you, hoping Heaven would discern and honor my utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 而奉被還詔，未蒙酬察，徒塵聖覽，仰延優旨，顧影慚惶，罔識攸厝。

translations.literal: Yet I received in turn an edict of return, not granted responsive examination — merely dusting the sacred gaze, looking up to extended gracious words; looking at my shadow, ashamed and alarmed, not knowing where to place myself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I received in reply an edict that did not answer my plea — my words merely troubled Your Majesty's eye while you extended gracious words to me; looking at my own shadow, I am ashamed and alarmed, not knowing where to turn.

sentences.zh: 臣忝荷要重，四載于今，既違前史量力之誡，又微古人進賢之美，尸位固寵，日積官謗，旋觀周行，興愧已厚。

translations.literal: Your subject undeservedly bears heavy charge, four years to now — already violating the former histories' admonition to measure one's strength, and falling short of the ancients' beauty of advancing the worthy; corpse in place, holding fast to favor, daily accumulating official slander — turning to look at my colleagues, shame already grows heavy.
translations.idiomatic: I have undeservedly borne weighty office for four years now — already violating the admonition of the histories to know one's limits, and falling short of the ancients' ideal of advancing the worthy. I have clung to my post and my favor, and official scandal accumulates day by day; looking at my colleagues around me, my shame is already deep.

sentences.zh: 況在親賢，朝野歸德，甫思引身，曷云能補，惟塵大典，虧喪已多。

translations.literal: How much more when a kinsman of worth — court and countryside return virtue to him — has just thought to withdraw himself; how could one say he can supply the lack? Only the dust on the great canon — loss and ruin already much.
translations.idiomatic: Now that a worthy kinsman has the devotion of court and countryside, the moment I thought to withdraw, how could I hope to make good the loss? I have already blemished the great enterprise in countless ways.

sentences.zh: 不悟天眷之隆，復垂恩奬，名器弗改，蒙寵如舊，愚惑自揆，[14]茫若無涯。

translations.literal: Not aware of Heaven's favor's loftiness, again bestowing grace and reward — name and regalia unchanged, receiving favor as before; foolish and confused in self-examination, [14] vast as without bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet unaware of how great Heaven's favor has been, you again bestowed grace upon me — my titles unchanged, favored as before — and in my foolish confusion I find myself, [14] lost as though in boundless darkness.

sentences.zh: 臣義康既總錄百揆，毗讚盛化，忝廁下風，諮憑有所。

translations.literal: Your subject Yikang already oversees the hundred affairs, aids and praises glorious transformation — I undeservedly stand in his leeward, consultation and reliance having its basis.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yikang already oversees all affairs of state and supports your glorious rule, I can humbly stand in his lee and turn to him for counsel when needed.

sentences.zh: 內朝細務，庶可免竭，神州任重，望實兼該，臣何人斯，寇竊不已。

translations.literal: Inner court minor affairs — perhaps one can avoid exhaustion; the heartland's charge weighty, reputation and reality both encompassing — what kind of person is your subject, bandit usurping without cease?
translations.idiomatic: Minor affairs of the inner court I might perhaps manage without exhausting myself, but the heartland carries weighty responsibility and demands both reputation and real ability — who am I to go on usurping a post I do not deserve?

sentences.zh: 為尒推遷，覆敗將及，就無人事之愆，必有陰陽之患。

translations.literal: For this reason procrastinating — overturning ruin will soon arrive; even if there were no human affairs' fault, there would surely be yin and yang's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I go on procrastinating, and ruin draws near; even if no human fault were involved, calamity of yin and yang would surely follow.

sentences.zh: 伏念惟憂，疢如疾首，不知何理，可以自安。

translations.literal: Prostrate in thought, only worry — affliction like disease in the head; not knowing by what principle one can find self-repose.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate in reflection, my worry is like a sickness in the head; I cannot see by what right I might rest at ease.

sentences.zh: 但成旨已決，渙汗難反，加臣懦劣，少無此志，進不能抗言陳辭，以死自固，退不能重繭置冰，鮮食為瘠，祗畏天威，遂復俛仰。

translations.literal: Yet the accomplished decree is already settled — sweat flowing is hard to reverse; added to your subject's cowardice and inferiority, little of this will; advancing cannot speak boldly and state words, using death to hold firm; retreating cannot wrap cocoon and set ice, fresh food becoming lean — only revering Heaven's majesty, thereupon again bowing up and down.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your decree had already been settled and could not easily be reversed; added to my own cowardice and weakness — I had little of such resolve — I could not advance to speak boldly and hold my ground even unto death, nor retreat to wrap myself in cocoon or walk on ice until I grew thin from fasting. Reverent before Heaven's majesty, I could only bow once more in submission.

sentences.zh: 至於攝督所部，料綜文案，曹局吏役，所須不多，其餘文武，皆為宂長。

translations.literal: As for supervising and directing my department, reviewing documents — bureau clerks and attendants needed are not many; the rest, civil and military, are all redundant chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: As for supervising my own staff and reviewing documents, the bureau clerks and attendants I need are not many; the rest of my civil and military officials are all superfluous.

sentences.zh: 相府初建，或有未充，請留職僚同事而已，自此以外，及諸資實，一送司徒。

translations.literal: The chief minister's headquarters newly established — perhaps not yet full; I request only retaining staff colleagues for shared work; apart from this, and all various resources and supplies, all send to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chief minister's headquarters has only just been established and may not yet be fully staffed, I ask only to retain enough colleagues for daily work; everything else, including all resources and supplies, I would send to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 臣受恩深重，休戚是預，義無虛飾，苟自貶損。

translations.literal: Your subject receiving grace deep and heavy, joy and sorrow shared therein — righteousness has no empty ornament, merely self-diminishment.
translations.idiomatic: Having received your grace so deeply, sharing in your joys and sorrows, I cannot offer empty ceremony — I speak only to diminish myself.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖察，特垂許順，不令誠訴，見其抑奪。」

translations.literal: Prostrate I wish sacred examination, specially granting permission and accord, not allowing sincere petition to see its suppression and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will discern my sincerity and grant my request, and not let my honest plea be set aside.

sentences.zh: [15]上又詔曰：「衞軍表如此，司徒宜須事力，可順公雅懷，割二千人配府。

translations.literal: [15] The emperor again edicted saying: "The General of the Guard's memorial thus — the Minister of Education should need manpower; one may follow my lord's refined wish, cutting two thousand men assigned to the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: [15] The emperor again issued an edict: "The General of the Guard's memorial reads as follows. The Minister of Education will need staff; in deference to your refined wishes, two thousand men may be cut from your staff and assigned to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 資儲不煩事送。」

translations.literal: Resources and stores — no need to trouble sending them."
translations.idiomatic: As for resources and stores, do not trouble yourself to send them."

sentences.zh: 弘博練治體，留心庶事，斟酌時宜，每存優允。

translations.literal: Hong was broadly versed in governing principles, attentive to various affairs, weighing the times' needs, always preserving generous approval.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was thoroughly versed in the principles of governance, attentive to everyday affairs, weighing each situation on its merits, and always inclined toward generous approval.

sentences.zh: 與八座丞郎疏曰：「同伍犯法，無士人不罪之科，然每至詰謫，輒有請訴。

translations.literal: In a letter to the eight chief seats and department directors and gentlemen he said: "When members of the same ward violate the law, there is no statute punishing men of the gentry class, yet whenever interrogation and reproof arrive, there are always pleas and petitions.
translations.idiomatic: In a letter to the heads of the chief ministries and their department directors, he wrote: "When members of the same household register violate the law, there is no statute that punishes men of the gentry class directly, yet whenever punishment is imposed, appeals are always lodged.

sentences.zh: 若垂恩宥，則法廢不可行；

translations.literal: If grace is extended in pardon, then the law is abandoned and cannot be enforced;
translations.idiomatic: If mercy is granted, the law becomes unenforceable;

sentences.zh: 依事糾責，則物以為苦怨。

translations.literal: If according to the matter one investigates and reproves, then people regard it as bitter resentment.
translations.idiomatic: if punishment is imposed according to the law, people complain bitterly.

sentences.zh: 宜更為其制，使得優苦之衷也。

translations.literal: One ought to make a new regulation for it, enabling the balanced mean of generous and bitter.
translations.idiomatic: A new regulation should be created that strikes a fair balance between leniency and severity.

sentences.zh: [16]又主守偷五匹，常偷四十匹，並加大辟，議者咸以為重，宜進主守偷十匹、常偷五十匹死，四十匹降以補兵。

translations.literal: [16] Further, stealing five bolts for a chief keeper, forty bolts for an ordinary keeper — both add capital execution; discussants all regarded it as heavy; one ought to advance to ten bolts death for chief keeper, fifty bolts death for ordinary keeper, forty bolts reduced to military conscription.
translations.idiomatic: [16] He also noted that stealing five bolts was punishable by death for a chief storekeeper and forty bolts for an ordinary keeper — punishments all agreed were too severe. He proposed raising the threshold to ten bolts for a chief keeper and fifty for an ordinary keeper before imposing death, with theft of forty bolts reduced to conscription as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 既得小寬民命，亦足以有懲也。

translations.literal: Having obtained a small easing of the people's lives, it is also sufficient to have warning.
translations.idiomatic: This would slightly ease the burden on the people while still serving as a deterrent.

sentences.zh: 想各言所懷。」

translations.literal: I would have each speak what he holds in mind."
translations.idiomatic: I would like each of you to state your views."

sentences.zh: 左丞江奧議：「士人犯盜贓不及棄市者，刑竟，自在贓汙淫盜之目，清議終身，經赦不原。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director Jiang Ao argued: "When men of the gentry commit theft and embezzlement not reaching abandonment in the market, once punishment is finished, they still fall under the category of embezzlement, corruption, and excessive theft — pure criticism for life, even through amnesty not restored.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director Jiang Ao argued: "When a man of the gentry commits theft or embezzlement short of execution, once his sentence is served he still falls under the category of corrupt theft — he bears the stain of public censure for life, and amnesty does not restore him.

sentences.zh: 當之者足以塞愆，聞之者足以鑒誡。

translations.literal: Those who receive it are sufficient to block fault; those who hear it are sufficient to mirror warning.
translations.idiomatic: Those who suffer this penalty have their guilt answered, and those who hear of it receive a sufficient warning.

sentences.zh: 若復雷同羣小，謫以兵役，愚謂為苦。

translations.literal: If again alike in thunder the petty crowd, relegating to military service — I foolishly deem it bitter.
translations.idiomatic: If members of the same register were again treated alike and relegated to military service along with common offenders, I believe that would be unduly harsh.

sentences.zh: 符伍雖比屋鄰居，至於士庶之際，實自天隔，舍藏之罪，無以相關。

translations.literal: Register wards though neighboring house to house — as for the boundary between gentry and commoners, in truth Heaven separates them; crimes of harboring and concealing have no basis for mutual connection.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the same register may be neighbors under the same roof, but between gentry and commoners the gap is as wide as heaven itself; the crime of harboring stolen goods cannot reasonably connect them.

sentences.zh: 奴客與符伍交接，有所藏蔽，可以得知，是以罪及奴客。

translations.literal: Slaves and clients intersect with register wards; if there is concealment it can be known — thus punishment reaches slaves and clients.
translations.idiomatic: When slaves and retainers interact with members of the register, any concealment can be discovered — that is why punishment may reach slaves and retainers.

sentences.zh: 自是客身犯愆，非代郎主受罪也。

translations.literal: From this it is the client's person committing fault — not on behalf of the gentleman master receiving punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In such cases it is the retainer himself who commits the offense — not the gentleman master who suffers punishment on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 如其無奴，則不應坐。」

translations.literal: If he has no slaves, then he ought not be implicated."
translations.idiomatic: If a gentleman has no retainers, he should not be implicated."

sentences.zh: 右丞孔默之議：「君子小人，既雜為符伍，不得不以相檢為義。

translations.literal: Right Assistant Director Kong Mozhi argued: "Gentlemen and petty men, already mixed as register wards — one cannot but take mutual inspection as principle.
translations.idiomatic: Right Assistant Director Kong Mozhi argued: "Gentlemen and commoners are already mixed within the same household registers, and mutual supervision is unavoidable in principle.

sentences.zh: 士庶雖殊，而理有聞察，譬百司居上，所以下不必躬親而後同坐。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners though different, yet reason has hearing and inspection — as when the hundred offices sit above, those below need not personally attend before shared imputation.
translations.idiomatic: Though gentry and commoners differ, principle still requires oversight — just as when the hundred offices sit in authority above, those below need not be personally involved to share liability.

sentences.zh: 是故犯違之日，理自相關。

translations.literal: Therefore on the day of violation and breach, reason naturally connects together.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when an offense is committed, liability naturally extends to those connected by register.

sentences.zh: [17]今罪其養子、典計者，蓋義存戮僕。

translations.literal: [17] Now punishing his adopted son and steward — probably the principle preserves punishing servants.
translations.idiomatic: [17] To punish a gentleman's adopted son or steward is essentially to maintain the principle of holding servants accountable.

sentences.zh: 如此，則無奴之室，豈得宴安。

translations.literal: If so, then a household without slaves — how could it rest at ease?
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, then how could a household without slaves rest at ease?

sentences.zh: 但既云復士，宜令輸贖。

translations.literal: Yet since it is said to restore the gentleman, one ought to make him pay ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the gentleman is to be restored to status, he should be allowed to pay a fine in redemption.

sentences.zh: 常盜四十匹，主守五匹，降死補兵。

translations.literal: For ordinary theft, forty bolts; for a chief storekeeper, five bolts — death reduced to conscription as a soldier.
translations.idiomatic: For ordinary theft, the threshold would be forty bolts; for a chief storekeeper, five bolts — with the death penalty reduced to conscription as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 雖大存寬惠，以紓民命，然官及二千石及失節士大夫，時有犯者，罪乃可戮，恐不可以補兵也。

translations.literal: Although greatly preserving generous favor to ease the people's lives, yet officials down to the two-thousand-dan rank and gentry who have lost integrity — when such sometimes offend, the crime is worthy of execution; I fear they cannot be made military conscripts.
translations.idiomatic: Although much is done to show leniency and ease the burden on common people, officials of rank and gentry who have lost their integrity do sometimes offend — their crimes merit execution, and I fear they should not be reduced to conscription.

sentences.zh: 謂此制可施小人，士人自還用舊律。」

translations.literal: I say this regulation may be applied to commoners; men of the gentry should return to the old law."
translations.idiomatic: This regulation may be applied to commoners; for men of the gentry, the old law should still apply."

sentences.zh: 尚書王准之議：「昔為山陰令，士人在伍，謂之押符。

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Wang Zhunzhi argued: "Formerly when I was Magistrate of Shanyin, gentlemen enrolled in the household register were called register-pledges.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Masters of Writing Wang Zhunzhi argued: "When I served as Magistrate of Shanyin, gentlemen enrolled in the household register were called register-pledges.

sentences.zh: 同伍有愆，得不及坐，士人有罪，符伍糾之。

translations.literal: When someone in the same ward had fault, he could avoid joint punishment; when a gentleman had guilt, the register ward investigated him.
translations.idiomatic: When a fellow member of the register committed an offense, a gentleman could avoid joint punishment; but when a gentleman himself committed an offense, the register ward would investigate him.

sentences.zh: 此非士庶殊制，實使即刑當罪耳。

translations.literal: This was not a separate system for gentry and commoners — it actually made punishment fit the crime.
translations.idiomatic: This was not a separate legal regime for gentry and commoners — it simply ensured that punishment matched the offense.

sentences.zh: 夫束脩之冑，與小人隔絕，防檢無方，宜及不逞之士，事接羣細，既同符伍，故使糾之。

translations.literal: Now, men who have received the bundle-and-sash — they are insulated from commoners, and prevention and inspection have no fixed method; it is fitting that when unrestrained gentlemen have dealings touching petty affairs, since they share the register ward, they should be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Men who have passed through formal schooling are insulated from commoners, and there is no ready way to supervise them. When unrestrained gentlemen become involved in petty affairs, since they are on the same register ward, it is only right that they be investigated.

sentences.zh: 于時行此，非唯一處。

translations.literal: At that time this was practiced — not in only one place.
translations.idiomatic: At that time this practice was not limited to a single locality.

sentences.zh: 左丞議奴客與鄰伍相關，可得檢察，符中有犯，使及刑坐。

translations.literal: The Left Assistant Director argued that bond-servants and guests are linked to neighboring wards and can be inspected; when there is an offense in the register, make them reach penal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Assistant Director argued that bond-servants and retainers are connected to neighboring ward registers and can therefore be supervised; when an offense appears on the register, their masters should bear criminal liability.

sentences.zh: 即事而求，有乖實理。

translations.literal: Seeking by the actual matter, this departs from real principle.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by the facts of the matter, this departs from sound principle.

sentences.zh: 有奴客者，類多使役，東西分散，住家者少。

translations.literal: Those who have bond-servants and guests — mostly they dispatch them on errands, scattered east and west; few remain at home.
translations.idiomatic: Households with bond-servants and retainers mostly send them out on errands, scattering them far and wide; few remain at home.

sentences.zh: 其有停者，左右驅馳，動止所須，出門甚寡，典計者在家十無其一。

translations.literal: Of those who remain, attendants rush about left and right for every movement and stop; they go out very rarely; stewards at home — not one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who remain are kept running about on every errand and rarely leave the premises; stewards who actually stay at home are fewer than one in ten.

sentences.zh: 奴客坐伍，濫刑必眾，恐非立法當罪本旨。

translations.literal: Bond-servants and guests punished by ward liability — excessive punishments would surely be many; I fear this is not the original intent of legislation fitting crime to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing bond-servants and retainers through ward liability would inevitably multiply excessive punishments, and I fear this is not what the law intended when it required punishment to fit the crime.

sentences.zh: 右丞議士人犯偷，不及大辟者，宥補兵。

translations.literal: The Right Assistant Director argued that when gentlemen commit theft not reaching capital execution, pardon and military conscription.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Assistant Director argued that when a gentleman commits theft short of capital punishment, he should be pardoned from death but conscripted as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 雖欲弘士，懼無以懲邪。

translations.literal: Although wishing to magnify the gentry, I fear there is no means to punish wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Although the aim is to show mercy to men of the gentry, I fear there will be no means of deterring misconduct.

sentences.zh: 乘理則君子，違之則小人。

translations.literal: Following reason, one is a gentleman; violating it, one is a petty person.
translations.idiomatic: He who follows principle is a gentleman; he who violates it is a common offender.

sentences.zh: 制嚴於上，猶冒犯之，以其宥科，犯者或眾。

translations.literal: When the law is strict above, they still offend against it; because of its lenient statute, offenders may be many.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the law is strict, people still offend against it; because the penalty is lenient, offenders may become numerous.

sentences.zh: 使畏法革心，[18]乃所以大宥也。

translations.literal: Making them fear the law and reform their hearts — [18] that is how one greatly pardons.
translations.idiomatic: The purpose of leniency is to make offenders fear the law and reform their hearts — that is how one greatly pardons.

sentences.zh: 且士庶異制，意所不同。」

translations.literal: Moreover, gentry and commoners have different systems — their intentions are not the same."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, gentry and commoners are governed by different rules, and their situations are not alike."

sentences.zh: 殿中郎謝元議謂：「事必先正其本，[19]然後其末可理。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Attendants Xie Yuan argued saying: "Affairs must first set right the root, [19] then the branches can be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of Attendants Xie Yuan argued: "In any matter one must first set right the root,[19] and only then can the branches be ordered.

sentences.zh: 本所以押士大夫於符伍者，所以檢小人邪？

translations.literal: The root — binding gentlemen and great officers to the register ward — is it to inspect commoners?
translations.idiomatic: Is the purpose of binding gentlemen and officials to the register ward to supervise commoners?

sentences.zh: [20]為使受檢於小人邪？

translations.literal: [20] Or is it to make them subject to inspection by commoners?
translations.idiomatic: [20] Or is it to make them subject to inspection by commoners?

sentences.zh: [21]案左丞稱士庶天隔，[22]則士無弘庶之由，以不知而押之於伍，則是受檢於小人也。

translations.literal: [21] Examining the Left Assistant Director's saying that gentry and commoners are heaven-separated, [22] then gentlemen have no reason to magnify commoners; binding them to the ward out of ignorance — then they receive inspection by commoners.
translations.idiomatic: [21] The Left Assistant Director says gentry and commoners are as far apart as heaven and earth,[22] which gives gentlemen no reason to show commoners the same leniency. Yet if they are bound to the ward register without knowledge of commoners' affairs, they are made subject to supervision by commoners.

sentences.zh: 然則小人有罪，士人無事，僕隸何罪，而令坐之。

translations.literal: If so, when commoners have guilt and gentlemen have no affair — what crime have servants, that they should be made to share punishment?
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, when commoners are guilty and the gentleman himself is blameless, what crime have his servants committed that they should be punished for it?

sentences.zh: 若以實相交關，責其聞察，[23]則意有未因。

translations.literal: If by actual mutual connection one demands their awareness and inspection, [23] then the reasoning is not fully grounded.
translations.idiomatic: If one holds them liable on the ground of actual connection and demands that they keep watch,[23] the reasoning is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 名實殊章，公私異令，奴不押符，是無名也，民乏貲財，是私賤也。

translations.literal: Name and reality differ in their statutes; public and private differ in their orders; slaves do not pledge registers — that is no official status; the people who lack wealth are privately held in low status.
translations.idiomatic: Title and reality follow different rules, and public law and private status are not the same. Slaves are not enrolled on the register — they have no official standing; and the people who lack wealth are privately held in low status.

sentences.zh: 以私賤無名之人，豫公家有實之任，公私混淆，名實非允。

translations.literal: Using privately base, nameless persons to undertake the state's actual duties — public and private are confused; name and reality are not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: To assign privately held, unregistered persons to duties that properly belong to the public realm is to blur public and private law — the arrangement is neither proper in name nor in reality.

sentences.zh: 由此而言，謂不宜坐。

translations.literal: Speaking from this, I say they should not share punishment.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, I say they should not bear joint punishment.

sentences.zh: 還從其主，於事為宜。

translations.literal: Returning to follow their master — in the affair this is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The matter should be referred back to the master — that would be the proper course.

sentences.zh: 無奴之士，不在此例。

translations.literal: Gentlemen without slaves — they are not within this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen without slaves are not covered by this rule.

sentences.zh: 若士人本檢小人，則小人有過，己應獲罪，而其奴則義歸戮僕，然則無奴之士，未合宴安，使之輸贖，於事非謬。

translations.literal: If gentlemen originally inspected commoners, then when commoners have fault they themselves ought receive guilt, while their slaves — the principle returns to punishing servants; yet then gentlemen without slaves ought not rest at ease — making them pay ransom is not mistaken in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: If the original purpose was for gentlemen to supervise commoners, then when commoners offend the gentleman himself should be held liable, while his slaves should be punished according to the principle of holding servants accountable. But then a gentleman without slaves cannot simply rest at ease — requiring him to pay a fine in redemption would not be unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 二科所附，惟制之本耳。

translations.literal: The two statutes that attach — only the root of the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The two penalties that apply here concern only the fundamental structure of the law.

sentences.zh: 此自是辯章二本，欲使各從其分。

translations.literal: This naturally distinguishes and sets forth the two roots, wishing to make each follow its division.
translations.idiomatic: This is simply a matter of distinguishing the two basic categories and letting each follow its proper rule.

sentences.zh: 至於求之管見，宜附前科，區別士庶，於義為美。

translations.literal: As for seeking it in my narrow view — one ought to attach to the prior statute, distinguishing gentry and commoners; in principle this is excellent.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, one should follow the earlier statute and distinguish gentry from commoners — that would be fair in principle.

sentences.zh: 盜制，按左丞議，士人既終不為兵革，幸可同寬宥之惠，不必依舊律，於議咸允。」

translations.literal: On the theft regulation, following the Left Assistant Director's argument — since gentlemen ultimately are not made soldiers, fortunately they may share the generous pardon's grace; there is no need to follow the old law — in the discussion all agreed."
translations.idiomatic: On the theft statutes, following the Left Assistant Director's view: since gentlemen are never conscripted as soldiers in any case, they may as well share in the leniency proposed. There is no need to apply the old law — and on this point all present agreed."

sentences.zh: 吏部郎何尚之議：「按孔右丞議，士人坐符伍為罪，有奴罪奴，無奴輸贖。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel He Shangzhi argued: "Following Right Assistant Director Kong's argument — when gentlemen receive guilt through register ward liability, if they have slaves the slaves are punished; if no slaves, they pay ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel He Shangzhi argued: "Following Right Assistant Director Kong's proposal: when a gentleman is held liable through the register ward, if he has slaves the slaves are punished; if he has none, he pays a fine in redemption.

sentences.zh: 既許士庶緬隔，則聞察自難，不宜以難知之事，定以必知之法。

translations.literal: Since gentry and commoners are granted vast separation, then awareness and inspection are naturally difficult; one ought not use what is hard to know to fix what must be known by law.
translations.idiomatic: Since gentry and commoners are held to be widely separated, mutual awareness is naturally difficult. One should not impose a law requiring certain knowledge for what is in fact hard to know.

sentences.zh: 夫有奴不賢，無奴不必不賢。

translations.literal: Now, having slaves is not unworthy; lacking slaves is not necessarily not unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Having slaves does not make a man unworthy, and lacking slaves does not necessarily make him virtuous.

sentences.zh: 今多僮者傲然於王憲，無僕者怵迫於時網，是為恩之所霑，恒在程、卓，法之所設，必加顏、原，求之鄙懷，竊所未愜。

translations.literal: Now those with many servants are insolent before the royal statutes; those without servants are alarmed and pressed by the times' net — thus where grace moistens, it is always with Cheng and Zhuo; where law is set, it must fall on Yan and Yuan — seeking it in my base heart, I privately am not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Today those with many household slaves defy the royal statutes with impunity, while those without servants are trapped by the law — so mercy always falls on the Cheng and Zhuo, while punishment always falls on the Yan and Yuan. In my humble view, this is deeply unsatisfying.

sentences.zh: 謝殿中謂奴不隨主，於名分不明，誠是有理。

translations.literal: Supervisor Xie said slaves do not follow their master — in name and status it is unclear; truly there is reason.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Xie is right that slaves are not legally bound to their masters in the register system — there is real force to that objection.

sentences.zh: 然奴僕實與閭里相關，今都不問，恐有所失。
