translations.literal: Yet bond-servants and attendants in fact are connected to the neighborhood ward; now not questioning at all — I fear something is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yet servants and attendants are in fact connected to neighborhood ward registers, and if we ignore that entirely, something important may be lost.

sentences.zh: 意同左丞議。」

translations.literal: My intention agrees with the Left Assistant Director's argument."
translations.idiomatic: My view agrees with the Left Assistant Director's proposal."

sentences.zh: 弘議曰：「尋律令既不分別士庶，又士人坐同伍罹謫者，無處無之，多為時恩所宥，故不盡親謫耳。

translations.literal: Hong argued saying: "Examining the statutes and orders — they do not distinguish gentry and commoners; moreover, gentlemen punished through same-ward liability — there is no place without it; mostly they are pardoned by timely grace, so joint punishment is not fully applied.
translations.idiomatic: Hong argued: "The statutes do not distinguish gentry from commoners, and gentlemen punished through same-ward liability can be found everywhere — though in practice many are pardoned by imperial grace, so the full penalty is rarely imposed.

sentences.zh: 吳及義興適有許、陸之徒，以同符合給，二千石論啟丹書。

translations.literal: In Wu and Yixing there happened to be men of the Xu and Lu lineages, through same-register matching given up — the two-thousand-dan officers memorialized with red writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu and Yixing, members of the Xu and Lu clans were implicated through register liability and turned over for punishment; the provincial governors memorialized with documents in red ink.

sentences.zh: 己未間，會稽士人云十數年前，亦有四族坐此被責，以時恩獲停。

translations.literal: Between the jiwei years, men of the gentry in Kuaiji say that more than ten years ago, four clans also sat in this and were punished, but through timely grace obtained a stay.
translations.idiomatic: During the jiwei reign period, gentry in Kuaiji reported that more than ten years earlier four clans had been punished on the same grounds, but execution was stayed by imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 而王尚書云人舊無同伍坐，所未之解。

translations.literal: Yet Minister Wang says people in the past had no same-ward punishment — what I have not understood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Minister Wang claims that same-ward punishment did not exist in the past — a claim I do not understand.

sentences.zh: 恐莅任之日，偶不值此事故邪。

translations.literal: I fear on the day of assuming office, he by chance did not encounter this affair?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps during his tenure he simply never encountered such a case.

sentences.zh: 聖明御世，士人誠不憂至苦，然要須臨事論通，上干天聽為紛擾，不如近為定科，使輕重有節也。

translations.literal: The sage-bright governs the age; gentlemen truly need not fear extremity of bitterness — yet one must discuss and report on affairs as they arise; disturbing Heaven's hearing is turmoil — better to make a fixed statute nearby, enabling heavy and light to have measure.
translations.idiomatic: Under a sage emperor, gentlemen need not fear the worst, yet each case still requires individual consideration, and flooding the throne with petitions creates turmoil. It would be better to establish a fixed statute now so that penalties are consistent.

sentences.zh: 又尋甲符制，蠲士人不傳符耳，令史復除，亦得如之。

translations.literal: Again examining the household register system — it exempts gentlemen from transmitting registers only; clerks and dismissed officials may likewise do so.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the household register system again, gentlemen are merely exempt from transmitting their registers personally; clerks and dismissed officials enjoy the same exemption.

sentences.zh: 共相押領，有違糾列，了無等衰，非許士人閭里之外也。

translations.literal: Mutually pledging and leading, with violation investigated and listed — utterly no gradation; it is not permitted that gentlemen are outside the neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the register mutually guarantee one another and are investigated when violations occur — there is no gradation of liability, and gentlemen are not exempt from neighborhood obligations.

sentences.zh: 諸議云士庶緬絕，不相參知，則士人犯法，庶民得不知。

translations.literal: The various arguments say gentry and commoners are vastly separated and do not mutually know — then when gentlemen violate the law, can commoners not know?
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that gentry and commoners are vastly separated and have no knowledge of one another — yet if that were so, would commoners truly be unaware when gentlemen break the law?

sentences.zh: 若庶民不許不知，何許士人不知。

translations.literal: If commoners are not permitted not to know, why permit gentlemen not to know?
translations.idiomatic: If commoners may not plead ignorance, why should gentlemen be allowed to?

sentences.zh: 小民自非超然簡獨，永絕塵粃者，比門接棟，小以為意，終自聞知，不必須日夕來往也。

translations.literal: Petty people — unless they are lofty, simple, and solitary, forever cutting off dust and filth — doors adjacent, eaves connecting; a little attention, ultimately they hear and know themselves; daily evening coming and going is not necessarily required.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners, unless they live in utter seclusion, live door to door and eave to eave; with a little attention they will eventually learn what is happening around them — daily contact is not required.

sentences.zh: 右丞百司之言，粗是其況。

translations.literal: The Right Assistant Director's words in the hundred offices — roughly this is the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Assistant Director's account of office practice broadly reflects the reality.

sentences.zh: 如衰陵士人，實與里巷關接，[24]相知情狀，乃當於冠帶小民。

translations.literal: Such as declining gentry — in fact they connect with lanes and alleys, [24] mutually knowing circumstances — they should be like capped-and-girdled petty people.
translations.idiomatic: Declining gentry in particular are in fact connected to their lanes and alleys,[24] well aware of local circumstances — they should be treated like any other registered commoner.

sentences.zh: 今謂之士人，便無小人之坐；

translations.literal: Now calling them gentlemen, they immediately have no commoner's punishment;
translations.idiomatic: If we call a man a gentleman, he is immediately exempt from the commoner's penalty;

sentences.zh: 署為小民，輒受士人之罰。

translations.literal: Enrolled as petty people, they immediately receive the gentleman's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: yet if he is registered as a commoner, he immediately receives the gentleman's penalty.

sentences.zh: 於情於法，不其頗歟？

translations.literal: In feeling and in law — is this not rather much?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not contrary to both reason and law?

sentences.zh: 且都令不及士流，士流為輕，則小人令使徵預其罰，便事至相糾，閭伍之防，亦為不同。

translations.literal: Moreover, the capital ordinance does not reach the gentry stream; the gentry stream is treated lightly — then the petty ordinance makes them levied into their punishment; then affairs reach mutual investigation — the neighborhood ward's defense is also different.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, capital ordinances do not apply to the gentry class, who are treated leniently — yet common ordinances make them share in punishment. This creates mutual denunciation and undermines the purpose of ward liability.

sentences.zh: 謂士人可不受同伍之讁耳，罪其奴客，庸何傷邪？

translations.literal: I say gentlemen may not receive same-ward reproof only; punishing their bond-servants and guests — what harm?
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen need only be exempt from direct ward punishment; punishing their bond-servants and retainers — what harm is there in that?

sentences.zh: 無奴客，可令輸贖，又或無奴僮為眾所明者，官長二千石便當親臨列上，依事遣判。

translations.literal: Without bond-servants and guests, one may make them pay ransom; furthermore, when there are no slave attendants known to all, the officer of rank two-thousand-dan ought personally to come and list upward, sending judgment according to the affair.
translations.idiomatic: If he has no bond-servants or retainers, he may pay a fine in redemption; or if everyone knows he has no slaves, the two-thousand-dan official should personally investigate and render judgment according to the facts.

sentences.zh: 又主偷五匹，常偷四十匹，[25]謂應見優量者，實以小吏無知，臨財易昧，或由疏慢，事蹈重科，求之於心，常有可愍，故欲小進匹數，寬其性命耳。

translations.literal: Again, chief theft five bolts, ordinary theft forty bolts — [25] those said to deserve favorable measure — in fact petty clerks are ignorant, facing wealth easily deluded, or perhaps through carelessness affairs tread heavy statutes; seeking in the heart, there is often pity; thus wishing slightly to advance the bolt count, easing their lives only.
translations.idiomatic: As for the five-bolt threshold for chief storekeepers and forty bolts for ordinary theft,[25] the proposed leniency is meant for petty clerks who, ignorant and tempted by opportunity, or through carelessness commit offenses punishable by death — offenses that often inspire pity. The intent was merely to raise the threshold slightly and spare their lives.

sentences.zh: 至於官長以上，荷蒙祿榮，付以局任，當正己明憲，檢下防非，而親犯科律，亂法冒利，五匹乃已為弘矣。

translations.literal: As for officers and above — bearing salary and glory, entrusted with office duties — they ought to rectify themselves and clarify statutes, inspect subordinates and prevent wrong; yet personally violating codes and laws, disordering law and seizing profit — five bolts already is magnanimous.
translations.idiomatic: As for officials of rank and above, who enjoy salary and honor and are entrusted with public office — they should discipline themselves, uphold the law, and supervise their subordinates. When they personally violate the law for profit, leniency at five bolts is already generous enough.

sentences.zh: 士人無私相偷四十匹理，就使至此，致以明罰，固其宜耳，並何容復加哀矜。

translations.literal: Gentry have no principle of privately stealing forty bolts with each other; even if it reached this, imposing clear punishment would be fitting indeed — how could one further add pity?
translations.idiomatic: There is no reason for a gentleman to steal forty bolts on his own account; even if a case reached that threshold, clear punishment would be entirely appropriate — how could further leniency be justified?

sentences.zh: 且此輩士人，可殺不可讁，有如諸論，本意自不在此也。

translations.literal: Moreover, this crowd of gentlemen — they may be killed but not reproved; as the various arguments say, the original intent was naturally not here.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, these gentlemen may be executed but should not be publicly reproved — as the various memorials show, that was never the point under discussion.

sentences.zh: 近聞之道路，聊欲共論，不呼乃爾難精。

translations.literal: Recently hearing it on the road, I merely wished to discuss together — not calling it forth, yet thus difficult to refine.
translations.idiomatic: I recently heard discussion of this on the street and merely wished to join the debate — without formal convocation, the matter is hard to resolve with precision.

sentences.zh: 既眾議糾紛，將不如其已。

translations.literal: Since the crowd's arguments are tangled and disputed, perhaps it is better to let it rest.
translations.idiomatic: Since opinions are so tangled, perhaps it would be better to let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 若呼不應停寢，謂宜集議奏聞，決之聖旨。」

translations.literal: If not calling it forth should not stop and rest, I say one ought to gather discussion and memorialize upward, deciding by sacred edict."
translations.idiomatic: If the debate cannot simply be dropped, I propose that the matter be referred for collective discussion and memorialized to the throne for imperial decision."

sentences.zh: 太祖詔：「衞軍議為允。」

translations.literal: The Founder edicted: "The General of the Guard's argument is approved."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu issued an edict: "The General of the Guard's proposal is approved."

sentences.zh: 弘又上言：「舊制，民年十三半役，十六全役。

translations.literal: Hong again submitted saying: "The old system — at age thirteen the people half-service, at sixteen full service.
translations.idiomatic: Hong submitted another memorial: "Under the old system, commoners performed half corvée duty at age thirteen and full duty at sixteen.

sentences.zh: 當以十三以上，能自營私及公，故以充役。

translations.literal: It should be that from thirteen and above, able to manage private and public on their own — thus used to fill service.
translations.idiomatic: The assumption was that from age thirteen a person could manage private and public affairs on his own and was therefore fit for corvée.

sentences.zh: 而考之見事，猶或未盡。

translations.literal: Yet examining actual affairs, perhaps still not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in practice this has not always proved to be the case.

sentences.zh: 體有強弱，不皆稱年。

translations.literal: Bodies have strong and weak; not all match their years.
translations.idiomatic: Physical strength varies, and not all match their age.

sentences.zh: 且在家自隨，力所能堪，不容過苦。

translations.literal: Moreover, at home following themselves, strength able to bear — cannot tolerate excessive bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: At home, each person works at his own pace and bears only what he can — the labor cannot be excessive.

sentences.zh: 移之公役，動有定科，循吏隱恤，可無其患，庸宰守常，已有勤劇，況值苛政，豈可稱言。

translations.literal: Moving to public service, movement has fixed statutes; conscientious officials hide compassion — perhaps without this trouble; mediocre magistrates keep convention — already have toil and severity; moreover encountering harsh government — how can it be spoken?
translations.idiomatic: Public corvée follows fixed quotas. A conscientious official may show compassion, but a mediocre magistrate simply follows convention — and the burden is already severe. Under harsh administration, the suffering is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 乃有務在豐役，增進年齒，孤遠貧弱，其敝尤深。

translations.literal: Then there are those whose task is abundant service, advancing age — isolated, distant, poor, weak — their harm especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials inflate corvée quotas and advance people's registered ages; the isolated, distant, and poor suffer most deeply.

sentences.zh: 至令依寄無所，生死靡告，一身之切，逃竄求免，家人遠討，胎孕不育，巧避羅憲，實亦由之。

translations.literal: Until making dependents without place, life and death with no report — the body's urgency, fleeing and hiding seeking escape; family members distantly pursued; fetuses and pregnancy not nurtured; cunning avoidance of nets and statutes — in fact also from this.
translations.idiomatic: People are left with nowhere to turn; life and death go unreported. Desperate individuals flee to escape service; families are hunted down from afar; pregnancies miscarry; and cunning evasion of the law — all stem from this.

sentences.zh: 今皇化惟新，四方無事，役召之宜，[26]應存乎消息。

translations.literal: Now imperial transformation is newly renewed, the four quarters without affairs — the fitness of service summons, [26] ought to rest in message and rest.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the imperial order is newly restored and the realm is at peace, corvée requirements[26] should be calibrated accordingly.

sentences.zh: 十五至十六，宜為半丁，十七為全丁。」

translations.literal: Fifteen to sixteen ought to be half laborer; seventeen full laborer."
translations.idiomatic: Ages fifteen and sixteen should count as half laborers; seventeen as full laborers."

translations.literal: [27] It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: [27] The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 其後弘寢疾，弘表屢乞骸骨，上輒優詔不許。

translations.literal: After this Hong lay ill in bed; Hong repeatedly memorialized begging to retire with his bones; the emperor always graciously edicted not permitting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Hong fell seriously ill and repeatedly memorialized asking to retire; the emperor always issued gracious edicts refusing.

sentences.zh: 九年，進位太保，領中書監，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he advanced to Grand Mentor, holding Director of the Palace Secretariat; the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to Grand Mentor and Director of the Palace Secretariat; his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其年，薨。

translations.literal: That year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he died.

sentences.zh: 時年五十四。

translations.literal: At the time age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 即贈太保、中書監，給節，加羽葆、鼓吹，增班劍為六十人，侍中、錄尚書、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Immediately posthumously granted Grand Mentor, Director of the Palace Secretariat, given staff, added feather canopy and martial pipes, increased halberd guard to sixty men — Attendant-in-Ordinary, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Mentor and Director of the Palace Secretariat, presented with the imperial staff, feather canopy, and martial pipes, and given a guard of sixty halberds; his posts as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector remained as before.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文昭公。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wenzhao Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Duke Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 配食高祖廟廷。

translations.literal: Shared sacrifice in the Founder's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a place in the sacrificial rites at Emperor Gaozu's temple.

sentences.zh: 其年，詔曰：「乃者三逆煽禍，實繁有徒，爰初遵養，暨于明罰，外虞內慮，實惟艱難。

translations.literal: That year, an edict said: "Recently the three rebels fanned calamity — truly many were their followers; from the first observing nurture unto clear punishment, external worry and internal anxiety — truly only difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict declared: "When the three rebels recently fanned rebellion, their followers were many indeed. From initial restraint through to open punishment, we faced threats abroad and anxiety at home — a time of genuine hardship.

sentences.zh: 故太保華容縣公弘、故衞將軍華、故左光祿大夫曇首，抱義懷忠，乃情同至，籌謀廟堂，竭盡智力，經綸夷險，[28]簡自朕心。

translations.literal: The late Grand Mentor, Duke of Huarong County Hong; the late General of the Guard Hua; the late Left Grand Master of the Bright Hou Tan Shou — embracing righteousness, cherishing loyalty, their feelings alike in utmost degree, planning in the temple hall, exhausting wisdom and strength, governing through peace and peril, [28] selected from my heart.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Mentor, Duke of Huarong, Hong; the late General of the Guard, Hua; and the late Left Grand Master of the Bright, Tan Shou — all embraced righteousness and loyalty with equal devotion, counseled in the throne room, and exhausted their wisdom and strength in steering the state through peril.[28] They were chosen from the bottom of my heart.

sentences.zh: 國恥既雪，允膺茅土，而並執謙挹，志不命踰，故用佇朝典，將有後命。

translations.literal: National shame already washed, duly receiving feudal soil — yet all holding humility and restraint, their will not exceeding command; therefore used to wait for court canon, about to have later appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When national humiliation was avenged, they were duly granted fiefs — yet all remained humble and refused to overstep their station. Accordingly they awaited further court appointments that were never issued.

sentences.zh: 盛業不究，相係殞落，永懷傷歎，痛恨無已。

translations.literal: Great enterprise not finished, successively falling — eternal remembrance wounded sigh, bitter hatred without end.
translations.idiomatic: Their great work unfinished, they fell one after another — my grief and bitter regret are endless.

sentences.zh: 弘可增封千戶，華、曇首封開國縣侯，食邑各千戶。

translations.literal: Hong may increase fief by one thousand households; Hua and Tan Shou enfeoffed as Marquis of a Founding County, fief each one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's fief was increased by one thousand households; Hua and Tan Shou were enfeoffed as founding marquises of a county, each with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍建昌公彥之，深誠密謨，比蹤齊望，其復先食邑，以酬忠勳。」

translations.literal: General Who Protects the Army, Duke of Jianchang Yanzhi — deep sincerity, secret counsel, matching traces with equal regard — restore his prior fief, to repay loyal merit."
translations.idiomatic: General Who Protects the Army, Duke of Jianchang, Yanzhi — who served with deep loyalty and secret counsel, equal to the others in merit — had his prior fief restored as reward for his service."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「聞王太保家便已匱乏，清約之美，同規古人。

translations.literal: Another edict: "Hearing that Grand Mentor Wang's household is already destitute — the beauty of pure economy, same standard as ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict stated: "I have heard that Grand Mentor Wang's household is already in want — the austerity of his life matched that of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 言念始終，情增悽歎。

translations.literal: Speaking and recalling beginning and end, feeling increased mournful sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on his lifelong devotion, my grief only deepens.

sentences.zh: 可賜錢百萬，米千斛。」

translations.literal: May grant money one million, rice one thousand hu."
translations.idiomatic: Let one million coins and one thousand hu of rice be granted to his household."

sentences.zh: 世祖大明五年，車駕遊幸，經弘墓。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, the imperial carriage toured, passing Hong's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming, Emperor Shizu passed Wang Hong's tomb during an imperial tour.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「故侍中、中書監、太保、錄尚書事、揚州刺史華容文昭公弘，德猷光劭，鑒識明遠。

translations.literal: An edict was issued saying: "The late Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Palace Secretariat, Grand Mentor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Inspector of Yangzhou, Duke Wenzhao of Huarong Hong — virtue and plan radiant and illustrious, discernment and knowledge bright and far.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued: "The late Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Palace Secretariat, Grand Mentor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yangzhou — Duke Wenzhao of Huarong, Hong — whose virtue and counsel were radiant, whose discernment was bright and far-reaching.

sentences.zh: 故散騎常侍、左光祿大夫、太子詹事豫寧文侯曇首，[29]夙尚恬素，理心貞正。

translations.literal: The late General of Cadet Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Grand Master of the Bright, Crown Prince's Chamberlain, Marquis Wen of Yunin Tan Shou — [29] from early esteemed pure simplicity, governing heart upright and correct.
translations.idiomatic: The late General of the Cadet Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Grand Master of the Bright, and Crown Prince's Chamberlain — Marquis Wen of Yunin, Tan Shou —[29] who from youth cherished simplicity and whose conduct was upright and principled.

sentences.zh: 並綢繆先眷，契闊屯夷，內亮王道，外流徽譽。

translations.literal: Both — intimate favor from the founder, parting through hardship together, inwardly illuminating the royal way, outwardly spreading fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Both enjoyed the founder's intimate favor, endured separation and hardship together, inwardly upheld the royal way, and outwardly won fine renown.

sentences.zh: 以國圖令勳，民思茂惠。

translations.literal: With the state's blueprint their merit, the people recall abundant grace.
translations.idiomatic: Their merit matched the state's design, and the people remember their abundant kindness.

sentences.zh: 朕薄巡都外，瞻覽墳塋，永言想慨，良深于懷。

translations.literal: I lightly tour outside the capital, viewing tombs and mounds — long speech and thought with sigh — truly deep in heart.
translations.idiomatic: On a brief tour outside the capital I viewed their tombs; my lasting remembrance and grief are truly deep in my heart.

sentences.zh: 便可遣使致祭墓所。」

translations.literal: At once may dispatch envoys to offer sacrifice at the tomb sites."
translations.idiomatic: Let envoys be sent at once to offer sacrifice at their tombs."

sentences.zh: 弘明敏有思致，既以民望所宗，造次必存禮法，凡動止施為，及書翰儀體，後人皆依倣之，謂為王太保家法。

translations.literal: Hong was bright, keen, and had thoughtful design; since the people's regard looked to him, in every circumstance he preserved ritual and law; every movement, conduct, letter, and formal style — later people all imitated them, calling it Grand Mentor Wang's household code.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was bright, keen, and thoughtful. As the people looked up to him, he unfailingly observed ritual and law in every circumstance. Every movement, action, letter, and formal gesture was imitated by later generations — they called it the household code of Grand Mentor Wang.

sentences.zh: 雖歷任藩輔，[30]不營財利，薨亡之後，家無餘業。

translations.literal: Although repeatedly serving as regional counselor, [30] not pursuing profit and wealth — after death, the household had no surplus estate.
translations.idiomatic: Although he served repeatedly as a regional counselor,[30] he never pursued profit; after his death his household had no surplus property.

sentences.zh: 而輕率少威儀，性又褊隘，人忤意者，輒面加責辱。

translations.literal: Yet rash and lacking dignified bearing; nature also narrow and intolerant — whoever crossed his will, he immediately face-to-face added blame and insult.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was rash and lacked dignified bearing; his nature was also narrow and intolerant — whoever crossed him he would immediately face and berate.

sentences.zh: 少時嘗摴蒲公城子野舍，及後當權，有人就弘求縣，辭訴頗切。

translations.literal: In youth he once played liubo at Ziye's lodge at Gongcheng; later when holding power, someone came to Hong seeking a county — pleading his case quite urgently.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he once played liubo at Ziye's lodge at Gongcheng; later when he held power, someone came to Hong seeking a county post and pleaded his case quite urgently.

sentences.zh: 此人嘗以蒲戲得罪，弘詰之曰：「君得錢會戲，何用祿為！」

translations.literal: This man once because of liubo play offended; Hong questioned him, saying: "You obtain money and know games — what use is salary!"
translations.idiomatic: This man had once offended through liubo gambling; Hong questioned him: "You know how to spend money on games — what need have you of a salary!"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「不審公城子野何在？」

translations.literal: He answered: "I do not know where Gongcheng Ziye is now?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "May I ask where Ziye of Gongcheng is now?"

sentences.zh: 弘默然。

translations.literal: Hong fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Hong fell silent.

sentences.zh: 子錫嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 少以宰相子，起家為員外散騎，歷清職，中書郎，太子左衞率，江夏內史。

translations.literal: From youth, as prime minister's son, began career as Supernumerary Cadet Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary; passed through pure offices — Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, Interior Administrator of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: As a prime minister's son, he began his career in youth as Supernumerary Cadet Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary; he passed through pure offices — Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, and Interior Administrator of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 高自位遇。

translations.literal: Highly self-regarding in rank and treatment.
translations.idiomatic: He held himself in high esteem for his rank and treatment.

sentences.zh: 太尉江夏王義恭當朝，錫箕踞大坐，殆無推敬。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Prince of Jiangxia Yigong held court; Xi sat with legs sprawled in great seat — scarcely any deferential respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Commandant Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, held court, Xi sat sprawling with legs spread — scarcely showing deference.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: Died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子僧亮嗣。

translations.literal: His son Sengliang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sengliang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，降爵為侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Qi received the abdication; rank reduced to marquis, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced to marquis with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 弘少子僧達，別有傳。

translations.literal: Hong's youngest son Sengda has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's youngest son Sengda has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 弘弟虞，廷尉卿。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Yu — Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's younger brother Yu served as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 虞子深，有美名，官至新安太守。

translations.literal: Yu's son Shen had a fine name; office reached Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Shen had a fine reputation and rose to Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 虞弟抑，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Yi — Grand Master for Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Yi served as Grand Master for Splendor.

sentences.zh: 抑弟孺，侍中。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Ru — Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Ru served as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 孺弟曇首，別有傳。

translations.literal: Ru's younger brother Tanshou has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's younger brother Tanshou has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 弘從父弟練，晉中書令珉子也。

translations.literal: Hong's paternal cousin Lian was son of Min, Central Secretariat Director of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's paternal cousin Lian was the son of Min, Central Secretariat Director of Jin.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，歷顯官，侍中，度支尚書。

translations.literal: During Yuanjia, passed through eminent offices — Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Masters of Writing for Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia he passed through eminent offices — Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing for Revenue.

sentences.zh: 練子釗，世祖大明中，亦經清職，黃門郎，臨海王子頊晉安王子勛征虜、前軍長史，左民尚書。

translations.literal: Lian's son Zhao — during Daming under Emperor Shizu also passed through pure offices: Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; Chief Clerk to the General Who Subdues Barbarians and to the Front Army under Prince Zixu of Linhai and Prince Zixun of Jin'an; Director of the Masters of Writing for the Left People.
translations.idiomatic: Lian's son Zhao — during Daming under Emperor Shizu also passed through pure offices: Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Chief Clerk to the General Who Subdues Barbarians and to the Front Army under Prince Zixu of Linhai and Prince Zixun of Jin'an, and Director of the Masters of Writing for the Left People.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong, served as Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Taizong's reign he served as Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 隨司徒建安王休仁出赭圻，時居母憂，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: Followed Minister of Education Prince of Jian'an Xiuren out to Zhechi; at the time in mourning for his mother, additionally made General Who Conquers Champions.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Minister of Education Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, out to Zhechi; at the time he was in mourning for his mother and was additionally made General Who Conquers Champions.

sentences.zh: 忤犯休仁，出為始興相。

translations.literal: Offended Xiuren; sent out as Chancellor of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Xiuren and was sent out as Chancellor of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 休仁恚之不已，太宗乃收付廷尉，賜死。

translations.literal: Xiuren's resentment toward him unceasing; Taizong then arrested and handed him to the Court of Justice, granting death.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren's resentment never ceased; Emperor Taizong then had him arrested and handed to the Court of Justice, and granted death.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉綱弛紊，其漸有由，孝武守文於上，化不下及，道子昏德居宗，憲章墜矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Jin's imperial framework slackened into disorder — the gradual process had its causes. Emperor Xiaowu above maintained the written tradition, yet transformation did not reach below; Daozi, of debased virtue, held the imperial lineage — laws and statutes fell away.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Jin's imperial order slackened into disorder, and the process had its causes. Emperor Xiaowu above preserved the written tradition, yet his influence never reached those below; Daozi, debased in virtue, held the imperial lineage, and the laws and statutes collapsed.

sentences.zh: 重之以國寶啟亂，加之以元顯嗣虐，而祖宗之遺典，羣公之舊章，莫不葉散冰離，掃地盡矣。

translations.literal: Compounded by Wang Guobao's instigation of rebellion, added to Sima Yuanxian's succession in cruelty — the ancestral codes and the ministers' old regulations, none escaped scattering like leaves or melting like ice; swept clean to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Compounded by Wang Guobao's instigation of rebellion and Sima Yuanxian's cruel succession, the ancestral codes and the ministers' old regulations scattered like leaves and melted like ice until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 主威不樹，臣道專行，國典人殊，朝綱家異，編戶之命，竭於豪門，王府之蓄，變為私藏。

translations.literal: Sovereign authority not established; ministerial conduct ran unchecked — state codes and human relations diverged, court norms and household customs differed. Registered households' lives were drained by great clans; princely storehouses became private hoards.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereign authority was not established and ministerial conduct ran unchecked. State codes and human relations diverged; court norms and household customs differed. The lives of registered households were drained by great clans, and princely storehouses became private hoards.

sentences.zh: 由是禍基東妖，難結天下，蕩蕩然王道不絕者若綖。

translations.literal: Hence the foundation of calamity arose in the east's sorcery; difficulties bound the realm — the kingly way, unbroken, hung as if by a single thread.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the foundation of calamity arose in the east's sorcery, and difficulties bound the realm — the kingly way hung by a thread as if on a single strand.

sentences.zh: 高祖一朝創義，事屬橫流，改亂章，布平道，尊主卑臣之義，定於馬棰之間。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor in one stroke raised righteous arms — the matter belonged to a torrential age. He mended disorder's statutes, spread the way of peace, and fixed the principle of honoring the sovereign and subordinating ministers between strokes of the riding crop.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor in one stroke raised righteous arms in a torrential age. He mended disorder's statutes, spread the way of peace, and fixed the principle of honoring the sovereign and subordinating ministers between strokes of the riding crop.

sentences.zh: 威令一施，內外從禁，以建武、永平之風，變太元、隆安之俗，此蓋文宣公之為也。

translations.literal: Authority and command once applied — inner and outer obeyed and were restrained; with the style of Jianwu and Yongping he transformed the customs of Taiyuan and Long'an. This was surely Duke Wenxuan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Once authority and command were applied, inner and outer obeyed and were restrained; with the style of Jianwu and Yongping he transformed the customs of Taiyuan and Long'an. This was surely the achievement of Duke Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 為一代宗臣，配饗清廟，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: As a pillar minister of the generation, sharing sacrifice in the Pure Temple — was it for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: As a pillar minister of his generation, honored with sacrifice in the Pure Temple — was it for nothing!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 且其勢亦美 「勢」各本並作「名」，據南史、元龜七二二改。

translations.literal: And moreover its situation is also fine: 'situation' in all editions reads 'name'; changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties and Yuan Gui 722.
translations.idiomatic: 'And moreover its situation is also fine': all editions read 'name' for 'situation'; corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties and Yuan Gui, juan 722.

sentences.zh: 自旦至日中 各本並脫「日」字，據南史、藝文類聚五八引、建康實錄、元龜三八八、七一八、八五０、御覽五九五引補。

translations.literal: From dawn to midday: all editions omit the character 'day'; supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties, Art and Literature Collection juan 58 citation, Veritable Record of Jiankang, Yuan Gui 388, 718, 850, and Imperial Readings juan 595 citation.
translations.idiomatic: 'From dawn to midday': all editions omit the character 'day'; supplemented from the History of Southern Dynasties, Art and Literature Collection juan 58, Veritable Record of Jiankang, Yuan Gui 388, 718, and 850, and Imperial Readings juan 595.

sentences.zh: 將軍尹領選如故 各本並脫「軍」字，據南史補。

translations.literal: General Yin continuing selection as before: all editions omit the character 'general'; supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'General Yin continuing selection as before': all editions omit the character 'general'; supplemented from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 甲仗五十人入殿 各本並脫「入殿」二字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Fifty sets of armor and weapons entering the hall: all editions omit the two characters 'entering the hall'; supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Fifty sets of armor and weapons entering the hall': all editions omit the two characters 'entering the hall'; supplemented from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 故尚書左僕射前將軍臣穆之 「前將軍」各本並作「前軍將軍」，據南史刪「軍」字。

translations.literal: Former Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, General of the Van, your minister Muzhi: 'General of the Van' in all editions reads 'General of the Front Army'; deleted the character 'army' according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Former Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, General of the Van, your minister Muzhi': all editions read 'General of the Front Army' for 'General of the Van'; the character 'army' was removed per the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「是前將軍，誤多軍字。」

translations.literal: Sun Biao's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: "It is General of the Van — the character 'army' was added in error."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Biao's Critical Study of the Book of Song observes: "The title is General of the Van — the character 'army' was added in error."

sentences.zh: 事隔於皇朝者 各本並脫「者」字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Matters separated from the imperial court by: all editions omit the character 'by'; supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Matters separated from the imperial court by': all editions omit the character 'by'; supplemented from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 南康國吏二百許人 「吏」各本並作「史」，據南史、元龜九二八、御覽七四二引改。

translations.literal: Two hundred or so clerks of the Principality of Nankang: 'clerks' in all editions reads 'histories'; changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties, Yuan Gui 928, and Imperial Readings juan 742 citation.
translations.idiomatic: 'Two hundred or so clerks of the Principality of Nankang': all editions read 'histories' for 'clerks'; corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties, Yuan Gui 928, and Imperial Readings, juan 742.

sentences.zh: 又有義宣故部曲潛於梁山洲外下投官軍 「有」疑當作「與」，或文有譌奪。

translations.literal: Again there were Yixuan's former retainers secretly outside Liangshan Isle going down to join the government army: 'there were' is suspected to read 'with,' or the text has corruption and omission.
translations.idiomatic: 'Again there were Yixuan's former retainers secretly outside Liangshan Isle going down to join the government army': 'there were' is suspected to read 'with,' or the text is corrupt and incomplete.

sentences.zh: 遂居劉安眾處 「劉」各本並作「留」，據南史、元龜九四四改。

translations.literal: Then occupied Liu An's crowd's place: 'Liu' in all editions reads 'remain'; changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties and Yuan Gui 944.
translations.idiomatic: 'Then occupied Liu An's crowd's place': all editions read 'remain' for 'Liu'; corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties and Yuan Gui 944.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「留當為劉，謂劉湛也。

translations.literal: Sun Biao's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: "Remain should be Liu — meaning Liu Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Biao's Critical Study of the Book of Song observes: "Remain should be Liu — meaning Liu Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛父柳，晉時封；

translations.literal: Zhan's father Liu was enfeoffed in Jin times;
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's father Liu was enfeoffed in Jin times;

sentences.zh: 湛襲封安眾男爵。」

translations.literal: Zhan inherited the enfeoffment as Baron of Anzhong."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan inherited the enfeoffment as Baron of Anzhong."

sentences.zh: 按劉湛出繼伯父淡，襲封安眾縣五等男。

translations.literal: Note: Liu Zhan was adopted to his paternal uncle Dan and inherited the fifth-rank barony of Anzhong county.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Liu Zhan was adopted to his paternal uncle Dan and inherited the fifth-rank barony of Anzhong county.

sentences.zh: 而府資役單刻 各本並脫「役」字，據元龜五０三補。

translations.literal: Yet the headquarters' labor resources were scant: all editions omit the character 'labor'; supplemented according to Yuan Gui 503.
translations.idiomatic: 'Yet the headquarters' labor resources were scant': all editions omit the character 'labor'; supplemented from Yuan Gui 503.

sentences.zh: 按府資單刻，謂軍府資望不足。

translations.literal: Note: headquarters resources scant means the military headquarters' prestige was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Note: 'headquarters resources scant' means the military headquarters' prestige was insufficient.

sentences.zh: 府資役單刻，謂軍府役力不足。

translations.literal: Headquarters labor resources scant means the military headquarters' labor power was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: 'Headquarters labor resources scant' means the military headquarters' labor power was insufficient.

sentences.zh: 驃騎府不得謂資望不足，故當加「役」字。

translations.literal: The Cavalry General's headquarters cannot be said to have insufficient prestige; therefore the character 'labor' should be added.
translations.idiomatic: The Cavalry General's headquarters cannot be said to have insufficient prestige; therefore the character 'labor' should be added.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞都亭侯王准之 「王准之」三朝本、北監本、毛本、殿本、局本並作「王淮之」。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Attendants, Marquis of Duting, Wang Zhunzhi: 'Wang Zhunzhi' in the Three Dynasties edition, Northern Directorate edition, Mao edition, Palace edition, and Bureau edition all read 'Wang Huaizhi'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Supervisor of Attendants, Marquis of Duting, Wang Zhunzhi': the Three Dynasties, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions all read 'Wang Huaizhi'.

sentences.zh: 按三朝本所據宋本殘葉，本作「王准之」。

translations.literal: Note: the Song fragment on which the Three Dynasties edition is based originally read 'Wang Zhunzhi'.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the Song fragment on which the Three Dynasties edition is based originally read 'Wang Zhunzhi'.

sentences.zh: 張元濟校勘記云：「當作王准之，見傳二十。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanji's collation note says: "It should read Wang Zhunzhi, as seen in Biography 20."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanji's collation note states: "It should read Wang Zhunzhi, as seen in Biography 20."

sentences.zh: 及影印百衲本時，襄校事者又據誤本改成「王淮之」。

translations.literal: When the photolithographic patchwork edition was produced, those assisting in collation again changed it to 'Wang Huaizhi' based on the erroneous text.
translations.idiomatic: When the photolithographic patchwork edition was produced, those assisting in collation again changed it to 'Wang Huaizhi' based on the erroneous text.

sentences.zh: 今改正。

translations.literal: Now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Now corrected.

sentences.zh: 元龜五一八亦作「王准之」不誤。

translations.literal: Yuan Gui 518 also reads 'Wang Zhunzhi' without error.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gui 518 also reads 'Wang Zhunzhi' without error.

sentences.zh: 「准」本作「準」，以宋順帝諱，改作「准」。

translations.literal: The graph zhun was originally the full-form graph; because of Emperor Shun of Song's taboo, it was changed to the simplified graph.
translations.idiomatic: The graph zhun was originally the full-form graph; because of Emperor Shun of Song's taboo, it was changed to the simplified graph.

sentences.zh: 光隆中興 各本並脫「中興」二字，據元龜三三二補。

translations.literal: Glorious restoration: all editions omit the two characters 'restoration'; supplemented according to Yuan Gui 332.
translations.idiomatic: 'Glorious restoration': all editions omit the two characters 'restoration'; supplemented from Yuan Gui 332.

sentences.zh: 宜入秉朝政翊贊皇猷竟陵衡陽春秋已長又宜出據列蕃齊光魯衞 各本並脫「宜入秉朝政

translations.literal: Ought to enter and hold court governance, assist and support the imperial design; Princes of Jingling and Hengyang, their years already grown; again ought to go out and occupy the various fiefs, equal to the glory of Lu and Wei: all editions omit 'ought to enter and hold court governance'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Ought to enter and hold court governance, assist and support the imperial design; Princes of Jingling and Hengyang, their years already grown; again ought to go out and occupy the various fiefs, equal to the glory of Lu and Wei': all editions omit 'ought to enter and hold court governance'.

translations.literal: 〈to〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈to〉

sentences.zh: 春秋已長又」共十八字，據建康實錄補。

translations.literal: Their years already grown, again' — eighteen characters in all; supplemented according to the Veritable Record of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: 'Their years already grown, again' — eighteen characters in all; supplemented from the Veritable Record of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 愚惑自揆 「愚惑」各本並作「感愚」，永樂大典卷六八三一作「感恩」，元龜三三一作「愚惑」。

translations.literal: Foolish and perplexed, self-examining: 'foolish and perplexed' in all editions reads 'moved and foolish'; Yongle Encyclopedia juan 6831 reads 'grateful'; Yuan Gui 331 reads 'foolish and perplexed'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Foolish and perplexed, self-examining': all editions read 'moved and foolish' for 'foolish and perplexed'; Yongle Encyclopedia juan 6831 reads 'grateful'; Yuan Gui 331 reads 'foolish and perplexed'.

sentences.zh: 今據元龜改。

translations.literal: Now changed according to Yuan Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Now corrected from Yuan Gui.

sentences.zh: 見其抑奪 「見其」各本並作「其見」，據元龜三三一改正。

translations.literal: Seeing his suppression and seizure: 'seeing his' in all editions reads 'his seeing'; corrected according to Yuan Gui 331.
translations.idiomatic: 'Seeing his suppression and seizure': all editions read 'his seeing' for 'seeing his'; corrected from Yuan Gui 331.

sentences.zh: 使得優苦之衷也 「優」各本並作「憂」，據元龜六一五改。

translations.literal: So as to enable the expression of heartfelt hardship: 'expression' in all editions reads 'anxiety'; changed according to Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: 'So as to enable the expression of heartfelt hardship': all editions read 'anxiety' for 'expression'; corrected from Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 理自相關 各本並脫「相」字，據元龜六一五補。

translations.literal: Principle naturally mutually connected: all editions omit the character 'mutually'; supplemented according to Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: 'Principle naturally mutually connected': all editions omit the character 'mutually'; supplemented from Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 使畏法革心 「革」各本並作「其」，據元龜六一五改。

translations.literal: Make them fear the law and reform their hearts: 'reform' in all editions reads 'their'; changed according to Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: 'Make them fear the law and reform their hearts': all editions read 'their' for 'reform'; corrected from Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 事必先正其本 「事必先正」四字，宋本空格，弘治本、北監本、毛本、殿本、局本作「宜先治」三字，今據元龜六一五補。

translations.literal: Affairs must first rectify the root — the four characters 'affairs must first rectify': in the Song edition a blank space; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read the three characters 'ought first govern'; now supplemented according to Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: 'Affairs must first rectify the root': the four characters 'affairs must first rectify' are blank in the Song edition; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read the three characters 'ought first govern'; now supplemented from Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 本所以押士大夫於符伍者所以檢小人邪 「押」各本並作「探」，據元龜六一五改。

translations.literal: The root reason for binding gentlemen and officials to the register ward is to inspect commoners for wrong, is it not: 'bind' in all editions reads 'probe'; changed according to Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: 'The root reason for binding gentlemen and officials to the register ward is to inspect commoners for wrong, is it not': all editions read 'probe' for 'bind'; corrected from Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 「伍者所」三字，宋本殘葉空白，弘治本、北監本、毛本、殿本、局本作「而末所」三字，今據元龜六一五補。

translations.literal: The three characters 'ward groups what': in the Song fragment a blank space; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read the three characters 'and end what'; now supplemented according to Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: The three characters 'ward groups what' are blank in the Song fragment; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read the three characters 'and end what'; now supplemented from Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 為使受檢於小人邪 「為」字，宋本殘葉空白，弘治本、北監本、毛本、殿本、局本作「可」字，元龜六一五作「為」字。

translations.literal: To make them receive inspection from petty people for wrong: the character 'to make' — in the Song fragment a blank space; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read the character 'may'; Yuan Gui 615 reads the character 'to make'.
translations.idiomatic: 'To make them receive inspection from petty people for wrong': the character 'to make' is blank in the Song fragment; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read 'may'; Yuan Gui 615 reads 'to make'.

sentences.zh: 今據元龜補。

translations.literal: Now supplemented according to Yuan Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Now supplemented from Yuan Gui.

sentences.zh: 案左丞稱士庶天隔 「案左丞稱」四字，宋本殘葉空白，弘治本、北監本、毛本、殿本、局本作「士犯坐奴是」五字，今據元龜六一五補。

translations.literal: Note: the Left Assistant Director said gentlemen and commoners are separated by heaven — the four characters 'Note Left Assistant Director said': in the Song fragment a blank space; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read the five characters 'gentleman commits offense bond-servant is'; now supplemented according to Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: 'Note: the Left Assistant Director said gentlemen and commoners are separated by heaven': the four characters 'Note Left Assistant Director said' are blank in the Song fragment; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read the five characters 'gentleman commits offense bond-servant is'; now supplemented from Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 責其聞察 「責」各本並作「貴」，據元龜六一五改。

translations.literal: Blame their failure to investigate and report: 'blame' in all editions reads 'honor'; changed according to Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: 'Blame their failure to investigate and report': all editions read 'honor' for 'blame'; corrected from Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 實與里巷關接 「接」宋本殘葉空白，弘治本、北監本、毛本、殿本、局本作「通」，今據元龜六一五補。

translations.literal: In fact connected with lanes and alleys: 'connected' — in the Song fragment a blank space; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read 'communicate'; now supplemented according to Yuan Gui 615.
translations.idiomatic: 'In fact connected with lanes and alleys': 'connected' is blank in the Song fragment; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read 'communicate'; now supplemented from Yuan Gui 615.

sentences.zh: 又主偷五匹常偷四十匹 各本並作「偷五匹，四十匹」，據南史訂補。

translations.literal: Again chief theft five bolts, ordinary theft forty bolts: all editions read 'theft five bolts, forty bolts'; corrected and supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Again chief theft five bolts, ordinary theft forty bolts': all editions read 'theft five bolts, forty bolts'; corrected and supplemented from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 役召之宜 各本並脫「宜」字，據通典食貨典、元龜四八六補。

translations.literal: The propriety of corvée summons: all editions omit the character 'propriety'; supplemented according to the Treatises on Food and Commodities in the Comprehensive Institutions and Yuan Gui 486.
translations.idiomatic: 'The propriety of corvée summons': all editions omit the character 'propriety'; supplemented from the Treatises on Food and Commodities in the Comprehensive Institutions and Yuan Gui 486.

sentences.zh: 十七為全丁 各本並脫「丁」字，據南史、通典食貨典、元龜四八六補。

translations.literal: Seventeen makes a full adult male: all editions omit the character 'adult male'; supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties, Treatises on Food and Commodities in the Comprehensive Institutions, and Yuan Gui 486.
translations.idiomatic: 'Seventeen makes a full adult male': all editions omit the character 'adult male'; supplemented from the History of Southern Dynasties, Treatises on Food and Commodities in the Comprehensive Institutions, and Yuan Gui 486.

sentences.zh: 經綸夷險 宋本殘葉作「經囗囗險」，弘治本、北監本、毛本、殿本、局本作「經營艱險」，元龜二一八作「經綸夷險」。

translations.literal: Governing through peace and peril: the Song fragment reads 'governing □□ peril'; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read 'managing hardship and peril'; Yuan Gui 218 reads 'governing through peace and peril'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Governing through peace and peril': the Song fragment reads 'governing □□ peril'; the Hongzhi, Northern Directorate, Mao, Palace, and Bureau editions read 'managing hardship and peril'; Yuan Gui 218 reads 'governing through peace and peril'.

sentences.zh: 今據元龜補。

translations.literal: Now supplemented according to Yuan Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Now supplemented from Yuan Gui.

sentences.zh: 豫寧文侯曇首 「豫寧」各本並作「豫章」，據王曇首傳改正。

translations.literal: Marquis Wen of Yunin Tanshou: 'Yunin' in all editions reads 'Yuzhang'; corrected according to the biography of Wang Tanshou.
translations.idiomatic: 'Marquis Wen of Yunin Tanshou': all editions read 'Yuzhang' for 'Yunin'; corrected from the biography of Wang Tanshou.

sentences.zh: 按州郡志，豫章郡有豫寧縣，無豫章縣，作豫寧是。

translations.literal: Note: according to the Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies, Yuzhang commandery had Yunin county but no Yuzhang county — reading Yunin is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Note: according to the Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies, Yuzhang commandery had Yunin county but no Yuzhang county — reading Yunin is correct.

sentences.zh: 雖歷任藩輔 「藩輔」各本作「藩翰」，據南史改。

translations.literal: Although repeatedly serving as regional counselor: 'regional counselor' in all editions reads 'regional bulwark'; changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Although repeatedly serving as regional counselor': all editions read 'regional bulwark' for 'regional counselor'; corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties.
